definition_zh: 失事的船；残骸；事故；毁坏；使（船）失事
definition_en: a ship or vehicle destroyed in an accident, the broken remains of it, or to destroy something completely
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上，一艘龙骨断裂的船半埋进沙里
scene: 风暴过后的清晨，海边的浅滩上躺着一艘只剩骨架的船。Divers found a wreck from the last century near the harbour mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 wreck 是「失事的船；残骸」（第 1 个义项：在事故中被毁的船或车，以及它剩下的残骸）；句意为潜水员在港口入口附近发现一艘上个世纪失事的船。退潮沙滩上那艘断了龙骨的船，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wreck 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「残骸；碎片」
由 wreck 加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「打捞船的人；拆毁者」
由 wreck 加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「失事的；被毁的」

senses.title: The broken ship
senses.definition: a ship, car, or plane that has been badly damaged or destroyed in an accident, or what is left of it
senses.definitionCN: 在事故中严重损坏或被毁的船、车或飞机，也指其残骸
senses.example: Divers found a wreck from the last century near the harbour mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在港口入口附近发现一艘上个世纪失事的船。
senses.why: Wreck first named a ship driven onto rocks and broken, so the object that survives an accident came to be called by its story.
senses.whyCN: wreck 最初指被风浪推上礁石撞碎的船，于是「经历事故后剩下的东西」就用这个故事的名称来称呼。

senses.title: The crash itself
senses.definition: an accident in which a vehicle is badly damaged or someone is badly hurt
senses.definitionCN: 车辆严重损坏或有人受重伤的事故
senses.example: The road was closed for hours after a wreck involving three trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 三辆卡车相撞的事故后，那条路封闭了几个小时。
senses.why: Because a broken hull is the visible result of a crash, the word moved from the result to the event that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 因为破碎的船体是撞毁事件看得见的结果，这个词就从结果移到了造成结果的事件上。

senses.title: A person in pieces
senses.definition: someone whose health, nerves, or life has been ruined, often in the phrase a nervous wreck
senses.definitionCN: 健康、精神或生活被摧毁的人，常见于说法 a nervous wreck
senses.example: After two sleepless nights she was a nervous wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 两个不眠之夜后，她的精神彻底垮了。
senses.why: If a body can be broken like a ship on rocks, then the same image describes a person whose nerves have cracked.
senses.whyCN: 如果身体可以像触礁的船一样被撞碎，那么同一个意象就能形容精神开裂的人。

senses.title: To break something apart
senses.definition: to damage or destroy something completely, or to cause a ship to break up
senses.definitionCN: 彻底损坏或摧毁某物，或使船破裂失事
senses.example: The storm wrecked two fishing boats on the same night.
senses.exampleCN: 那一夜风暴让两条渔船失事。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to give something the fate of the broken ship is to wreck it.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了动词：让某物遭遇破船的命运，就是 wreck it。

senses.title: The ruined plan
senses.definition: to spoil or ruin something such as a plan, a chance, or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、机会或关系等破灭或遭到破坏
senses.example: Heavy rain wrecked our plans for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨毁了我们的野餐计划。
senses.why: Abstract things are treated like fragile vessels, so whatever breaks them is said to wreck them.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的东西被当作易碎的容器，于是毁掉它们就说成 wreck。

intro.en: Wreck came into English from Old Norse and is related to the idea of something driven ashore and broken; the modern noun and verb grew from that picture.
intro.cn: wreck 由古诺斯语进入英语，本义与被冲上岸、撞碎的东西有关；现代的名词与动词都是从这幅画面长出来的。

items.en: The verb rekja and the noun wreck meant to drive something, especially a ship, ashore.
items.cn: 动词 rekja 与名词 wreck 意为把东西（尤指船）冲到岸上。

items.en: wrak or wrek named goods and ships cast up on the shore after a storm.
items.cn: wrak 或 wrek 指风暴后冲上岸的货物与船只。

items.en: Coastal law spoke of wreckum, the right to claim what the sea threw up.
items.cn: 沿海法律里说 wreckum，指认领大海抛上岸之物的权利。

items.en: The meaning widened from stranded ships to any vehicle or person that has been ruined.
items.cn: 词义从搁浅的船扩大到任何被毁的车辆或人。

items.en: The verb to wreck, meaning to ruin, is a later back-formation from the noun.
items.cn: 表示毁坏的动词 wreck 是由名词后期反向构成的。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same seamanship family, the second holds other words for ruin and disaster.
note.cn: 第一组收同一航海词族里的词，第二组收其他表示毁灭与灾难的词。

entries.definition: The broken parts left after a wreck.
A person or vehicle that clears away wrecks.
Destroyed or badly damaged.
To spoil or destroy something completely.
Scattered pieces left after something is destroyed.
The body of an old or broken ship.

normalIntro.en: Wreck is one syllable and starts with wr, the old English spelling habit that keeps the r silent.
normalIntro.cn: wreck 只有一个音节，以 wr 开头，这是英语里 r 不发音的老拼写习惯。

normal.en: The wr at the start is silent in the r, as in write and wrong.
normal.cn: 开头的 wr 里 r 不发音，write 与 wrong 也是这样。

normal.en: The same word gives shipwreck and wreckage.
normal.cn: 同一个词构成 shipwreck 与 wreckage。

normal.en: A nervous wreck borrows the image of a ship broken on rocks.
normal.cn: nervous wreck 借的是触礁碎船的意象。

normal.en: Wreck as a verb means to ruin, as in wreck the plan.
normal.cn: wreck 作动词意为毁掉，如 wreck the plan。

normal.en: Wreck is related to the Old Norse verb rekja, to drive ashore.
normal.cn: wreck 与古诺斯语动词 rekja（冲上岸）有关。

abstract.en: A broken keel sticking out of wet sand at low tide.
abstract.cn: 退潮时从湿沙里露出的断裂龙骨。

abstract.en: The silence after the wave has finished throwing things around.
abstract.cn: 浪把东西抛完之后的那片安静。

abstract.en: Something that once moved now lying still in pieces.
abstract.cn: 曾经会动的东西如今碎着躺下不动。

examples.en: The wreck of an old fishing boat was still visible at low tide.
examples.cn: 退潮时仍能看见一艘旧渔船的残骸。

examples.en: Two drivers were hurt in the wreck on the motorway.
examples.cn: 高速公路上的车祸中有两名司机受伤。

examples.en: The storm wrecked the harbour wall and flooded the village.
examples.cn: 风暴毁坏了码头墙，淹了村子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克」——礁石来克船，船就被克得只剩骨架。

root: 源自中古英语 wrak、wrek，来自古诺斯语 *wrek，本义为「被冲上岸的东西、漂来的残骸」，与 rekja（冲、赶）同源；同族词有 wreckage、wrecked。

sensesIntro.en: The broken ship comes first, then the crash that broke it, then the ruined person, then the act of ruining anything, then ruined plans.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有破碎的船，再有撞碎它的事故，然后是垮掉的人，接着是毁掉任何东西的动作，最后是破灭的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken hull half buried in sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：半埋在沙里的破碎船体。

branches.en: The object branch: what is left of the ship.
branches.cn: 实物分支：船剩下的东西。

branches.en: The event branch: the crash that produced the wreck.
branches.cn: 事件分支：造成残骸的那场撞毁。

branches.en: The human branch: a body broken like a ship.
branches.cn: 人分支：像船一样被撞碎的身体。

branches.en: The action branch: giving something the fate of a ship on rocks.
branches.cn: 动作分支：让某物经历触礁的船那样的命运。

branches.en: The image branch: both a ship and a person can end up in pieces.
branches.cn: 意象分支：船和人最后都可能碎成一堆。

intro.en: Wreck is a free stem borrowed from Old Norse; English added -age, -er and -ed to build the family around it.
intro.cn: wreck 是从古诺斯语借入的自由词干，英语在它周围加上 -age、-er、-ed 建成词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Norse, not Latin, so no Latin ancestor exists; the entries below are distant Indo-European cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自诺斯语而非拉丁语，因此没有拉丁语祖先；下面几条只是印欧语系的远亲。

items.meaning: the broken ship and the act of breaking
items.meaningCN: 破碎的船与毁坏的动作
items.example: The stem carries both the object and the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干同时承载物与动作。

items.example: Ship names the vessel and wreck names its fate.
items.exampleCN: ship 指明船只，wreck 指明它的命运。

items.meaning: a mass or collection of things
items.example: It forms wreckage, the mass of broken parts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wreckage，指成堆的残骸。

items.example: It forms wrecker, one who clears wrecks.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrecker，清理残骸的人。

items.example: It forms wrecked, having been destroyed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrecked，被毁的。

items.example: The wrecked car blocked the lane.
items.exampleCN: 被撞毁的车堵住了车道。

items.meaning: the act of destroying or the moment of a crash
items.meaningCN: 毁坏的动作或撞毁的时刻
items.example: They cleared the wrecking site at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时清理了撞毁现场。

items.example: It is a different second element, but the sound recalls wreck.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分是不同的词，但读音让人想起 wreck。

definition_zh: 手腕；腕关节；（衣袖的）腕部
definition_en: the joint or narrow part of the body between the hand and the forearm
core_image: 伸手接过一杯热水时，袖子下面露出的那圈细窄关节
scene: 冬天出门前，老人把围巾拉紧，又把袖口重新拢好。She twisted her wrist trying to open the stiff jar.
sceneCN: 这里 wrist 是「手腕」（第 1 个义项：手与前臂之间那个关节和细窄部位）；句意为她想拧开那个拧不动的罐子，结果扭伤了手腕。接热水时袖子下露出的那圈细窄关节，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: wear a watch on your wrist

derivatives.zh: 由 wrist 加 band 复合构成，义为「腕带；腕套」
由 wrist 加指小后缀 -let 构成，义为「腕饰；腕带」
由 wrist 加 -y 构成，义为「用腕力的」

senses.title: The narrow joint
senses.definition: the joint between the hand and the forearm, and the narrow part of the arm just above the hand
senses.definitionCN: 手与前臂之间的关节，也指手部上方那段细窄的手臂
senses.example: She twisted her wrist trying to open the stiff jar.
senses.exampleCN: 她想拧开那个拧不动的罐子，结果扭伤了手腕。
senses.why: The word has named this joint since Old English, so the body part is the earliest and strongest meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古英语起就指这个关节，所以身体部位是最早也最牢固的意思。

senses.title: The edge of a sleeve
senses.definition: the part of a sleeve that covers or ends at the wrist
senses.definitionCN: 袖子覆盖腕部或到腕部为止的那一段
senses.example: He wiped his mouth on his wrist, forgetting there were paper towels.
senses.exampleCN: 他在手腕上擦了擦嘴，忘了有纸巾。
senses.why: Because clothing ends where the joint is, the name of the joint passed to the garment edge that reaches it.
senses.whyCN: 因为衣物正好止于这个关节，关节的名称就传给了伸到那里的那截袖边。

senses.title: The hand at work
senses.definition: the power and movement of the hand controlled from this joint, especially in sport
senses.definitionCN: 由这个关节控制的手部动作与力量，尤指运动中的腕力
senses.example: A good tennis player puts the whole wrist into the serve.
senses.exampleCN: 优秀的网球选手发球时用上整个手腕的力量。
senses.why: Once the joint is the hinge of the hand, the motion it makes can stand for skill itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个关节成了手的铰链，由它做出的动作就可以代表技巧本身。

senses.title: The gentle punishment
senses.definition: a small punishment or gentle warning, in the fixed phrase a slap on the wrist
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的惩罚或温和的警告，用于固定说法 a slap on the wrist
senses.example: The company got a slap on the wrist for the missing labels.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因标签缺失只受到轻微处罚。
senses.why: A slap on the wrist hurts a little but breaks nothing, so the phrase grew into a picture of lenient blame.
senses.whyCN: 打在手腕上有点疼却伤不了人，于是这个说法成了宽容责备的画面。

intro.en: Wrist is a native Germanic word built on a root that suggests twisting, a fitting name for the joint that turns the hand.
intro.cn: wrist 是本土的日耳曼词，词根有「扭转」的意思，用来称那个能转动手的关节十分贴切。

items.en: wrist named the joint of the hand in everyday and medical writing.
items.cn: wrist 在日常与医学文字里都指手上的关节。

items.en: The spelling settled as wrist, keeping the silent w before r.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 wrist，保留了 r 前那个不发音的 w。

items.en: The clothing sense, the part of a sleeve at the joint, appeared in the same period.
items.cn: 衣物义（袖子上到腕部的那一截）也在同一时期出现。

items.en: Compounds such as wristband and wristwatch spread the word into clothing and clocks.
items.cn: wristband、wristwatch 等复合词把它带进衣物与钟表。

items.en: The phrase a slap on the wrist became a standard image of lenient punishment.
items.cn: 说法 a slap on the wrist 成了宽容处罚的标准意象。

note.en: The first group holds words for the same joint area, the second holds neighbouring body parts.
note.cn: 第一组收同一关节部位的词，第二组收相邻的身体部位。

entries.definition: More than one wrist.
A band worn around the wrist.
A small band or ornament for the wrist.
The joint between the leg and the foot.
The joint in the middle of the arm.
A joint in a finger.

normalIntro.en: Wrist begins with the silent wr that English keeps in writing but drops in speech.
normalIntro.cn: wrist 以不发音的 wr 开头，英语写它、却不读那个 w。

normal.en: The w before r is silent, just as in write and wrong.
normal.cn: r 前的 w 不发音，正如 write 与 wrong。

normal.en: Wrist and write are both spelled with wr but have no shared meaning.
normal.cn: wrist 与 write 都写 wr，但意思毫无关系。

normal.en: Wristband is the band worn at the wrist.
normal.cn: wristband 就是系在腕上的带子。

normal.en: A slap on the wrist means a punishment that barely hurts.
normal.cn: a slap on the wrist 指几乎不疼的处罚。

normal.en: Watch the joint that turns the hand, and you have the wrist.
normal.cn: 盯着那个转动手的关节，那就是 wrist。

abstract.en: A thin ring of bare skin where the sleeve ends.
abstract.cn: 袖口结束时露出的那一圈细窄皮肤。

abstract.en: A wrist turning slowly to check the time.
abstract.cn: 慢慢转动手腕去看时间。

abstract.en: Something small but strong enough to carry a whole body.
abstract.cn: 很小，却结实得能托起整个身体。

examples.en: The nurse held his wrist and counted the beats.
examples.cn: 护士按住他的手腕数脉搏。

examples.en: These gloves are too short and leave the wrist bare.
examples.cn: 这副手套太短，把手腕露在外面。

examples.en: He broke his wrist falling off his bike.
examples.cn: 他从自行车上摔下来，手腕骨折了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞斯特」——表带在手腕上，斯特地提醒你看时间。

root: 古英语 wrist（腕），属日耳曼语族，与德语 Rist（手背、腕）同源，词根一般认为与「扭转」有关；同族词有 wristband、wristlet。

sensesIntro.en: The joint comes first, then the sleeve that reaches it, then the movement it controls, then the gentle punishment measured at the same place.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是关节，再是伸到关节处的袖边，然后是它控制的动作，最后是在同一处量出的轻微处罚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the narrow turning point between hand and arm.
core.cn: 核心意象：手与前臂之间那个细窄的转动点。

branches.en: The body branch: the joint where the hand turns.
branches.cn: 身体分支：手能转动的那处关节。

branches.en: The clothing branch: sleeves end where the joint is.
branches.cn: 衣物分支：袖子止于关节所在的位置。

branches.en: The skill branch: motion from this joint becomes wrist power.
branches.cn: 技巧分支：这里的动作变成腕力。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: a blow that lands here barely hurts.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：打在这里的惩罚几乎不疼。

branches.en: The image branch: a bare ring of skin between glove and sleeve.
branches.cn: 意象分支：手套与袖子之间露出的一圈皮肤。

intro.en: Wrist is a single native stem; English built wristband and wristlet by adding a free word and a small suffix.
intro.cn: wrist 是单一的本土词干；英语加一个独立词和小后缀构成 wristband 与 wristlet。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below belong to a related old medical family.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词属于相关的古老医学词族。

items.meaning: the joint between hand and arm
items.example: The stem carries the whole body meaning.
items.exampleCN: 词干承载了整个身体部位的意思。

items.example: It appears in write, wrong and wrist.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 write、wrong、wrist 里。

items.example: It gives wrists, the plural.
items.exampleCN: 它构成复数 wrists。

items.meaning: a band worn at the wrist
items.example: The band names what is worn.
items.exampleCN: band 指所戴的带子。

items.meaning: a small ornament for the wrist
items.example: The suffix -let marks something small.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -let 表示小而轻。

items.meaning: a watch worn on the wrist
items.example: The watch hangs at the wrist.
items.exampleCN: 表就挂在手腕上。

items.meaning: a light blow with the open hand
items.example: It explains why the punishment is mild.
items.exampleCN: 它解释了为什么这种处罚是轻的。

items.example: The adjective describes sports strokes.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词形容运动中的击球动作。

latinEntries.meaning: to pluck, to bend the wrist

definition_zh: 作家；作者；撰写者；写字的人
definition_en: a person who writes books, articles, or other texts, especially as a job
core_image: 窗边一张堆满纸的书桌，有人在上面一遍遍划掉又重写
scene: 午后的书桌上落着一层薄灰，稿纸摞得比水杯还高，键盘上几个字母已磨得发亮。The writer spent three years on the same novel.
sceneCN: 这里 writer 是「作家；作者」（第 1 个义项：以写书、写文章为业或擅长写作的人）；句意为这位作家在同一部小说上花了三年。窗边堆满纸的书桌与反复涂改的手，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 writer 加 -ly 构成，义为「作家式的；有文人气质的」
由 write 加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「写作；文字；作品」
由 writer 加 -ship 构成，义为「作家身份；写作职业」

senses.title: The maker of books
senses.definition: a person who writes books, stories, or articles, often as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 写书、写故事或写文章的人，常以写作为职业
senses.example: The writer spent three years on the same novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家在同一部小说上花了三年。
senses.why: The suffix -er turns the act of writing into the name of the person who does it, so the worker comes from the work.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 把写作这个动作变成做这件事的人，于是人从事情里长出来。

senses.title: The hand behind a text
senses.definition: the particular person who produced a given letter, report, or message
senses.definitionCN: 某一封信、报告或消息的具体写作者
senses.example: The writer of the letter never gave a name.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信的写信人始终没有留下姓名。
senses.why: Any text has an author behind it, so the word also fixes the single hand that made this one.
senses.whyCN: 任何文本背后都有作者，于是这个词也用来确定造就这一篇的那只手。

senses.title: The one who forms letters
senses.definition: someone who is writing or who writes in a particular way, without being an author
senses.definitionCN: 正在写字或以某种方式写字的人，不一定是作者
senses.example: Left-handed writers often turn the page slightly.
senses.exampleCN: 惯用左手写字的人常把纸斜一点。
senses.why: The plain action sense survives beside the professional one, because a person can write without writing books.
senses.whyCN: 不带职业色彩的动作义与职业义并存，因为一个人可以只写字而不写书。

senses.title: Something that writes
senses.definition: a thing that performs the action of writing, as in phrases about a good or bad writer of a pen
senses.definitionCN: 执行书写动作的物品，如说一支笔写得好或不好
senses.example: This old pen is a slow writer and leaves ink spots.
senses.exampleCN: 这支旧笔写起来很慢，还会漏墨点。
senses.why: Since -er can also mark a tool, an instrument may be called a writer by the action it performs.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -er 也可以指工具，所以器具可以按它做的事被叫作 writer。

intro.en: Writer is the English agent noun of write, built in the Middle English period with the ending -er that marks the doer.
intro.cn: writer 是 write 在英语内部构成的施动名词，中古英语时期加上表示「做某事的人」的 -er。

items.en: The verb writan already had related agent forms in use for scribes.
items.cn: 动词 writan 当时已有指抄写者的相关施动形式。

items.en: writere named anyone who writes, from a clerk to the author of a book.
items.cn: writere 指任何写字的人，从书记到书的作者。

items.en: Printing made books cheap and turned writer into a clear profession.
items.cn: 印刷让书变便宜，writer 也成了明确的职业名称。

items.en: Compounds such as songwriter and ghost writer spread the agent noun widely.
items.cn: songwriter、ghost writer 这样的复合词把这个施动名词推向各处。

items.en: Today the word covers novelists, journalists, and anyone who composes a text.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖小说家、记者以及任何写成一篇文章的人。

note.en: The first group gathers the write family, the second gathers words for those who produce texts.
note.cn: 第一组集合 write 的词族，第二组集合其他指写文章的人的词。

entries.definition: More than one writer.
To put words down in marks.
The act of writing or the text produced.
The person who wrote a book or started a plan.
A person who writes novels.
A person who writes news and reports.

normalIntro.en: Writer is simply write plus -er, so the spelling of write is kept whole before the ending.
normalIntro.cn: writer 就是 write 加 -er，因此词尾之前完整保留了 write 的拼写。

normal.en: Drop nothing when adding -er: write becomes writer.
normal.cn: 加 -er 时不用丢字母：write 就是 writer。

normal.en: The w stays silent, so the first syllable sounds like rye.
normal.cn: w 仍不发音，第一个音节读起来像 rye。

normal.en: A songwriter writes songs, and a ghost writer writes for someone else.
normal.cn: songwriter 写歌，ghost writer 替别人写。

normal.en: The -er ending marks the person who does the action.
normal.cn: 后缀 -er 标示做这个动作的人。

normal.en: Author is the Latin cousin used more in publishing.
normal.cn: author 是拉丁语系的近亲，在出版界更常用。

abstract.en: A desk covered with crossed-out pages.
abstract.cn: 一张铺满划掉稿纸的桌子。

abstract.en: One lamp still on after everyone else has gone to bed.
abstract.cn: 别人都睡下后仍亮着的一盏灯。

abstract.en: A voice that exists only on the page.
abstract.cn: 只存在于纸面上的一个声音。

examples.en: She became a writer after ten years as a teacher.
examples.cn: 当了十年老师后，她成了作家。

examples.en: The writer of the report asked for more time.
examples.cn: 这份报告的撰写人要求多给些时间。

examples.en: Writers often read their own sentences aloud to test them.
examples.cn: 写作者常把自己的句子读出声来检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞特」——稿纸堆成塔，瑞特是那个一直写到手酸的人。

root: 由动词 write（古英语 writan，刻划、书写）加施动后缀 -er 构成，字面义为「写字的人」，后专指以写作为业的人。

sensesIntro.en: The profession comes first, then the particular hand behind one text, then anyone forming letters, then even a pen doing the writing.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是职业，再是某篇文字背后的那只手，然后是任何写字的人，最后连笔也能被称作写者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a desk of crossed-out pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在铺满涂改稿纸的书桌前的人。

branches.en: The profession branch: writing as a life and a trade.
branches.cn: 职业分支：以写作为生活与营生。

branches.en: The attribution branch: the single hand behind this letter.
branches.cn: 归属分支：这封信背后的那只手。

branches.en: The plain action branch: anyone who writes, author or not.
branches.cn: 动作分支：任何写字的人，不论是否作者。

branches.en: The tool branch: a pen judged by how it writes.
branches.cn: 工具分支：以写得好坏来评断的笔。

branches.en: The identity branch: from doing the work to being known by it.
branches.cn: 身份分支：从事这件事，到以此为人所知。

intro.en: Writer is a transparent compound of the verb write and the agent suffix -er, and further endings build on it.
intro.cn: writer 由动词 write 加施动后缀 -er 清晰构成，它本身还能再带后缀。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic, so the English word has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below belong to the same old root family.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属日耳曼语，因此这个英语词没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词同属那个古老词根家族。

items.example: The base names the action.
items.exampleCN: 词基指明动作。

items.example: It turns write into writer.
items.exampleCN: 它把 write 变成 writer。

items.example: It gives writers for many of them.
items.exampleCN: 它构成复数 writers。

items.example: It forms writerly, like a professional writer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 writerly，有作家气派的。

items.example: It forms writership, the status of a writer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 writership，作家身份。

items.example: Song names what is written.
items.exampleCN: song 指明写的是什么。

items.meaning: a writer who writes for another name
items.example: The name on the cover is not the writer.
items.exampleCN: 封面上的名字并不是写的人。

items.example: Copy is the text of an advertisement.
items.exampleCN: copy 指广告文字。

definition_zh: 错误的；不对的；不合适的；错事；冤枉
definition_en: not correct or not true, not suitable, or to treat someone unfairly
core_image: 路牌指向岔路，走上去却发现前面是死胡同
scene: 岔路口的路牌被风吹歪了，一行人照着箭头走，最后停在断墙前。You have the wrong number, said a voice on the phone.
sceneCN: 这里 wrong 是「错误的；不对的」（第 1 个义项：不正确、不真实的）；句意为电话那头说「你打错号码了」。被风吹歪的路牌把行人引到断墙前，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wrong 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「错误地；不公正地」
由 wrong 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「不当的；非法的」
由 wrong 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「错误；不当」
由 wrong 与 doing 复合构成，义为「坏事；不法行为」

senses.title: Not correct
senses.definition: not correct, not true, or not matching the facts
senses.definitionCN: 不正确、不真实或与事实不符
senses.example: You have the wrong number, said a voice on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 电话那头有人说，你打错号码了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is twisted or crooked, and a crooked line is the plainest picture of something not straight, that is, not correct.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是「扭的、歪的」，歪斜的线就是「不正」最直白的画面，即不正确。

senses.title: Not the right one
senses.definition: not suitable for a particular person, time, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 对某个人、某个时间或某个用途不合适
senses.example: It was the wrong moment to ask for a raise.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时机提加薪是不合适的。
senses.why: If a thing is off the straight line, it is also off the fitting place, so unsuitability joins incorrectness.
senses.whyCN: 事物偏离直线，也就偏离了合适的位置，于是「不合适」与「不正确」并在一起。

senses.title: In the wrong way
senses.definition: in a way that is not correct, used as an adverb without -ly in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 以不正确的方式，日常口语中作副词而不加 -ly
senses.example: The spelling went wrong after the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 第一行之后拼写就出错了。
senses.why: English often lets the adjective stand as an adverb, so the crooked thing also describes how the action goes.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让形容词直接充当副词，于是「歪的东西」也用来形容动作的方式。

senses.title: Something done badly
senses.definition: an action that is bad, unfair, or against what is right
senses.definitionCN: 坏的、不公正的或违背正当之事的行为
senses.example: He could not forgive the wrong done to his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法原谅家人所受的冤屈。
senses.why: A crooked act is a wrong act, so the adjective hardened into a noun for the deed itself.
senses.whyCN: 歪的行为就是不正当的行为，于是形容词固化成指这种行为本身的名词。

senses.title: To treat unfairly
senses.definition: to treat someone unfairly or treat them as if they had done something bad
senses.definitionCN: 不公正地对待某人，或把坏事归到某人身上
senses.example: She felt wronged by the way the manager spoke to her.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得经理对她说话的方式冤枉了她。
senses.why: To do a wrong to someone is to make them the victim of the crooked act, so the noun turned into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 对某人做一件错事，就是让他成为歪行的受害者，于是名词又变成动词。

intro.en: Wrong came into English from Old Norse and started with the physical sense of twisted or crooked before it became moral.
intro.cn: wrong 由古诺斯语进入英语，先有「扭的、歪的」这个物理意义，之后才转向道德意义。

items.en: rangr meant twisted, bent out of shape, or contrary.
items.cn: rangr 意为扭的、变形的、反向的。

items.en: Wrong first described crooked things and crooked behaviour in the same breath.
items.cn: wrong 起初同时形容歪的东西与不正的行为。

items.en: The moral sense grew stronger, so wrong came to mean not right in conduct.
items.cn: 道德义逐渐加强，wrong 于是意指行为上不正当。

items.en: The adverb use without -ly settled in everyday speech.
items.cn: 日常口语固定了不加 -ly 的副词用法。

items.en: The verb to wrong, meaning to treat unfairly, comes from the noun.
items.cn: 表示不公正对待的动词 wrong 由名词而来。

note.en: The first group holds the family built on wrong, the second holds words that stand against right or fairness.
note.cn: 第一组收以 wrong 构成的词族，第二组收与「正当、公平」相对的词。

entries.definition: In a mistaken or unfair way.
Not fair or not legal.
Treated unfairly by someone.
Not correct or not true.
Wrong because of a mistake in thinking.
Not treating people equally or justly.

normalIntro.en: Wrong keeps the silent w and has no -ly adverb in ordinary speech, which makes it easy to spot in a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: wrong 保留不发音的 w，日常口语里作副词也不加 -ly，因此在句子里很好认。

normal.en: The w is silent, so wrong sounds like rong.
normal.cn: w 不发音，wrong 读起来像 rong。

normal.en: Go wrong means something turns out badly.
normal.cn: go wrong 指事情出了岔子。

normal.en: The wrong number is the phrase you hear on a misdialled phone.
normal.cn: wrong number 是打错电话时听到的那句话。

normal.en: Add -ly for the adverb wrongly, used in careful writing.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得副词 wrongly，多用于正式文字。

normal.en: The old meaning is twisted, which links wrong to crooked.
normal.cn: 旧义是「扭的」，这把 wrong 与「歪」连在一起。

abstract.en: A sign pointing into a dead end.
abstract.cn: 一块把路指向死胡同的牌子。

abstract.en: A line that will not stay straight no matter how you look at it.
abstract.cn: 无论怎么看都直不起来的一条线。

abstract.en: The moment you realise the key fits the wrong door.
abstract.cn: 你发觉钥匙插错了门的那一刻。

examples.en: I think you gave me the wrong address.
examples.cn: 我想你把地址给我错了。

examples.en: Something went wrong with the engine during the flight.
examples.cn: 飞行途中发动机出了问题。

examples.en: He apologised for wronging her in front of the team.
examples.cn: 他为在团队面前冤枉了她而道歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「荣昂」——调子唱得荣昂过头，就跑调跑错了。

root: 源自中古英语 wrong，来自古诺斯语 rangr（扭的、歪的、反向的），与 wrangle 有远亲关系；由「歪」引申为「不正确、不正当」。

sensesIntro.en: The crooked line comes first, then the misplaced thing, then the crooked way, then the crooked deed, then the person who suffers it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是歪的线，再是放错位置的东西，然后是歪的做法，接着是不正当的行为，最后是承受这种行为的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that bends away from the straight path.
core.cn: 核心意象：偏离直路的一条弯线。

branches.en: The truth branch: a claim that does not match the facts.
branches.cn: 真假分支：与事实不符的说法。

branches.en: The fit branch: a thing in the wrong place or time.
branches.cn: 适配分支：位置或时机不对的事物。

branches.en: The manner branch: the crooked line describes how something is done.
branches.cn: 方式分支：歪线用来形容做事的方式。

branches.en: The deed branch: the crooked act becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 行为分支：歪的行动固化成名词。

branches.en: The justice branch: from the deed to the person forced to bear it.
branches.cn: 公正分支：从行为到被迫承受它的人。

intro.en: Wrong is a single Norse stem that now carries adjective, adverb, noun, and verb uses; suffixes build the rest of its family.
intro.cn: wrong 是单一的诺斯语词干，如今兼作形容词、副词、名词和动词；其余词族靠后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Norse rather than Latin; the entries below are Latin words for crookedness and injustice, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自诺斯语而非拉丁语；下面几条是拉丁语中表示「歪」与「不义」的词，并非祖先。

items.example: The stem serves four parts of speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干可作四种词性。

items.example: It appears in wrong, write and wrist.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 wrong、write、wrist 里。

items.example: It forms wrongly, used in formal contexts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongly，多用于正式场合。

items.example: It forms wrongful, full of injustice.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongful，充满不义。

items.example: It forms wrongness, the state of being wrong.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongness，错误的状态。

items.example: Doing names the act, wrong describes it.
items.exampleCN: doing 指明行为，wrong 加以形容。

items.example: It forms wronger, rare but regular.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wronger，罕见但合乎规则。

items.example: It gives wrongs as a verb form and a noun plural.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词三单与名词复数。

definition_zh: 错误地；不正确地；不公正地；冤枉地
definition_en: in a way that is mistaken, incorrect, or unfair
core_image: 标签贴反了的东西，被放进了另一个箱子
scene: 仓库里一摞贴错标签的箱子被搬上了另一辆货车，收件人根本不在那一边。The parcel was wrongly sent to the old address.
sceneCN: 这里 wrongly 是「错误地；不正确地」（第 1 个义项：以搞错的方式）；句意为包裹被错误地寄到了旧地址。贴反标签、放进错箱子的东西，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wrongly 去掉后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「错误的；不对的」
由 wrong 加 -ful 构成，义为「不当的；非法的」
由 wrong 加 -ness 构成，义为「错误；不当」

senses.title: In a mistaken way
senses.definition: in a way that is not correct or not based on the facts
senses.definitionCN: 以不正确或不以事实为依据的方式
senses.example: The parcel was wrongly sent to the old address.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹被错误地寄到了旧地址。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the crooked adjective into a description of how an action is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把「歪的」形容词变成对动作如何进行的描述。

senses.title: In an unfair way
senses.definition: in a way that is unfair to someone or blames them without cause
senses.definitionCN: 以对某人不公或无缘无故指责的方式
senses.example: He was wrongly blamed for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的责任被错误地推到了他身上。
senses.why: A deed that bends away from right is also unfair, so the adverb covers unjust treatment as well as error.
senses.whyCN: 偏离正道的做法同时也是不公平的，于是这个副词既指错误也指不义的对待。

senses.title: With a wrong meaning
senses.definition: in a way that gives a false meaning to words or actions
senses.definitionCN: 以给词语或行为赋予错误含义的方式
senses.example: Her silence was wrongly read as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默被误读成了同意。
senses.why: When meaning itself goes crooked, the reader rather than the writer is the one who acts wrongly.
senses.whyCN: 当意思本身走歪时，错的是读者而不是写的人。

senses.title: Against the rules
senses.definition: in a way that breaks a rule or a proper procedure
senses.definitionCN: 以违反规则或正当程序的方式
senses.example: The form was wrongly completed, so it had to be redone.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表填得不合规定，只好重填。
senses.why: Rules draw straight lines, so anything done off the line is done wrongly in a procedural sense.
senses.whyCN: 规则画出直线，凡偏离这条线去做的，在程序意义上就是 wrongly。

intro.en: Wrongly is the adverb formed from the adjective wrong with the native ending -ly, which English has used this way since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: wrongly 是形容词 wrong 加本土后缀 -ly 构成的副词，英语自中世纪起就这样构词。

items.en: The base rangr meant twisted or contrary.
items.cn: 词基 rangr 意为扭曲的、反向的。

items.en: Wrong was used both as adjective and adverb, and -ly forms appeared beside it.
items.cn: wrong 兼作形容词与副词，旁边还出现带 -ly 的形式。

items.en: Wrongly specialised as the careful written adverb of error.
items.cn: wrongly 专门充当表示「错误」的书面副词。

items.en: Legal writing made wrongly accused and wrongly convicted fixed phrases.
items.cn: 法律文字让 wrongly accused 与 wrongly convicted 成了固定说法。

items.en: Everyday speech still prefers plain wrong, so wrongly sounds slightly formal.
items.cn: 日常口语仍偏爱不加 -ly 的 wrong，因此 wrongly 听起来略正式。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same family, the second holds adverbs of error and unfairness.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词族的形式，第二组收表示错误与不公的副词。

entries.definition: Not correct or not right.
Unfair or against the law.
The quality of being wrong.
Because of a mistake in thinking.
In a way that is not correct.
In a way that is not just.

normalIntro.en: Wrongly is wrong plus -ly: the silent w stays, and the ending tells you it describes an action.
normalIntro.cn: wrongly 是 wrong 加 -ly：不发音的 w 仍保留，词尾说明它修饰动作。

normal.en: Wrongly is the written adverb; plain wrong is the spoken one.
normal.cn: wrongly 是书面副词，口语里直接用 wrong。

normal.en: The phrase wrongly accused appears in news reports about courts.
normal.cn: wrongly accused 常出现在关于法庭的新闻报道里。

normal.en: The -ly ending never changes the silent w.
normal.cn: -ly 词尾不会改变不发音的 w。

normal.en: Wrongly blamed means the blame landed in the wrong place.
normal.cn: wrongly blamed 指责任落到了错的人身上。

normal.en: Use wrongly with past participles such as spelt and labelled.
normal.cn: wrongly 常与 spelt、labelled 等过去分词连用。

abstract.en: A label stuck on the wrong box.
abstract.cn: 贴在错误箱子上的标签。

abstract.en: A name crossed out on a form and replaced by another.
abstract.cn: 表格上一个被划掉、换成另一个的名字。

abstract.en: A quiet person hearing a verdict that describes someone else.
abstract.cn: 一个沉默的人听到了一段说的是别人的判词。

examples.en: The letter was wrongly addressed and came back a week later.
examples.cn: 这封信地址写错了，一周后被退回。

examples.en: He was wrongly accused of taking the money.
examples.cn: 他被冤枉拿了那笔钱。

examples.en: Several words in the sign were wrongly spelt.
examples.cn: 牌子上的几个词拼错了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「荣利」——追荣利追得太急，路就走歪了。

root: 由形容词 wrong（古诺斯语 rangr，扭的、歪的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面义为「以歪的方式」，即错误地、不公正地。

sensesIntro.en: A mistaken action comes first, then unfair treatment, then misread meaning, then broken procedure.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是做错的动作，再是不公的对待，然后是读错的意思，最后是违反的程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label stuck on the wrong box.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴在错误箱子上的标签。

branches.en: The error branch: action taken on false facts.
branches.cn: 错误分支：依据错误事实采取的行动。

branches.en: The justice branch: blame placed on the innocent.
branches.cn: 公正分支：责任落到无辜者身上。

branches.en: The meaning branch: words taken in a false sense.
branches.cn: 意义分支：词语被理解成错的意思。

branches.en: The procedure branch: a step taken off the straight line.
branches.cn: 程序分支：偏离直线的一步。

branches.en: The shared branch: both error and injustice start as a bent line.
branches.cn: 共同分支：错误与不公都始于一条弯线。

intro.en: Wrongly is a transparent adjective plus -ly; the base is a Norse stem that stays unchanged before the suffix.
intro.cn: wrongly 是形容词直接加 -ly 的透明结构；词基是诺斯语词干，加后缀前形状不变。

latinIntro.en: The base is not Latin, so the words below are related concepts rather than ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 词基并非拉丁语，因此下面这些词是相关概念而非祖先。

items.example: The base supplies the whole meaning.
items.exampleCN: 词基提供全部意义。

items.example: It changes the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成副词。

items.example: It forms wrongly blamed and wrongly accused.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongly blamed 与 wrongly accused。

items.example: Mistakenly carries the same idea from another prefix.
items.exampleCN: mistakenly 用另一个前缀表达同样的意思。

items.example: Unfairly is the close partner in the fairness sense.
items.exampleCN: unfairly 在「公平」义上是它的近邻。

items.example: It forms wrongness from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词干构成 wrongness。

items.example: It is the legal flavoured partner of wrongly.
items.exampleCN: 它是 wrongly 带法律色彩的同族副词。

items.example: The adverb often describes how such acts happen.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词常说明这类行为是怎样发生的。

definition_zh: 院子；庭院；场地；（工厂等的）堆场；码
definition_en: an open area beside or around a building, an enclosed area used for work, or a unit of length equal to about ninety centimetres
core_image: 屋后一圈矮栅栏，围出可以晾衣、堆柴、跑孩子的空地
scene: 雨停后，屋后的空地上积了一小滩水，孩子在栅栏边踩来踩去。My father keeps his old bicycle in the yard behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 yard 是「院子；庭院」（第 1 个义项：房屋旁边或四周的空地）；句意为父亲把旧自行车放在屋后的院子里。屋后矮栅栏围出的那块空地，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 yard 与 stick 复合构成，义为「码尺；衡量的标准」
由 farm 与 yard 复合构成，义为「农家的场院」
由 brick 与 yard 复合构成，义为「砖厂；制砖场地」

senses.title: The open ground by a house
senses.definition: a piece of open ground, often enclosed, beside or around a house or other building
senses.definitionCN: 房屋或其他建筑旁边或四周的一块空地，常用围墙围起
senses.example: My father keeps his old bicycle in the yard behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲把旧自行车放在屋后的院子里。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is an enclosed patch of ground, and the space fenced beside a dwelling is its most familiar form.
senses.whyCN: 词根最早的意思就是围起来的一块地，房屋旁边 fencing 出来的那块空间正是它最常见的样子。

senses.title: The working ground
senses.definition: an enclosed area used for a particular kind of work, such as storing goods, building ships, or sorting railway cars
senses.definitionCN: 为某种工作而围起来的场地，如堆放货物、造船或调度车辆
senses.example: Trucks waited in line outside the railway yard all night.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在铁路调车场外排了一整夜。
senses.why: Once ground is set aside and fenced, it can be filled with any work, so the enclosed patch shifts from home to industry.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把地圈起来围住，就可以用它做任何活计，于是围地这个词从家宅挪到了工业里。

senses.title: The long measure
senses.definition: a unit of length used in Britain and America, equal to three feet or about ninety centimetres
senses.definitionCN: 英美使用的长度单位，合三英尺，约九十厘米
senses.example: The dress needs two yards of blue cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子需要两码蓝布。
senses.why: The measuring sense probably began with a stick of fixed length kept in a yard, and the tool gave its name to the length.
senses.whyCN: 量长度的义项大概起源于院子里一根定长的木棍，工具的名字后来变成了长度的名字。

senses.title: The railway storage area
senses.definition: the part of a railway station where trains are stored, sorted, and made ready
senses.definitionCN: 火车站中存放、编组和准备列车的那片场地
senses.example: A long line of coal cars stood idle in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 长列煤车停在调车场里闲着。
senses.why: This is only a special case of the working ground, narrowed to the railway, where the ground is filled with rails instead of goods.
senses.whyCN: 这只是工作场地那个义项的专化，范围缩到铁路，不过地上铺满的是铁轨而不是货物。

senses.title: The home ground of an animal
senses.definition: an enclosed area where animals such as deer or poultry are kept
senses.definitionCN: 圈养鹿、家禽等动物的围起来的场地
senses.example: The deer browsed quietly in the fenced yard at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿在后边围起的场院里安静地吃草。
senses.why: An enclosure for animals is the same fenced patch moved outdoors, so the word widens from people to livestock.
senses.whyCN: 圈养动物的围地就是同一块围地在户外延伸，于是这个词从人扩展到了牲畜。

intro.en: Yard is an old Germanic word for an enclosed space, related to Dutch gaard and German Garten, all from a root meaning something fenced in.
intro.cn: yard 是古老的日耳曼语词，指围起来的空间，与荷兰语 gaard、德语 Garten 同源，都出自「被围住的东西」这个词根。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form meant a fenced enclosure, whether for people, animals, or plants.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式意为围起来的圈地，可以围人、围畜或围植物。

items.en: geard named an enclosed plot of ground, and the word appears in place names across England.
items.cn: 古英语 geard 指围起来的一块地，这个词出现在英格兰各地地名中。

items.en: The form settled as yard, still with the sense of an enclosed piece of ground.
items.cn: 形式固定为 yard，仍保持「围起来的一块地」的意思。

items.en: The word spread over any working ground, and the fixed stick in a yard gave Britain its measure of length.
items.cn: 这个词扩用到各种工作场地，而院子里那根定长木棍给了英国一个长度单位。

items.en: Compounds such as shipyard, farmyard, and brickyard keep the old enclosure sense alive.
items.cn: shipyard、farmyard、brickyard 这类复合词让古老的围地之义延续下来。

note.en: These words share the idea of ground, or are close in spelling to yard.
note.cn: 这些词要么与「地面、场地」的概念有关，要么在拼写上接近 yard。

entries.definition: a stick marked with units, used for measuring or for judging standards
entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词，码尺，也比喻衡量的标准

entries.definition: the area of ground around farm buildings
entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词，农家的场院

entries.definition: a piece of land where fruit trees are grown
entries.definitionCN: 同属「圈起来的园地」一类，果园

entries.definition: an enclosed area next to a building, or a place where a ball game is played
entries.definitionCN: 近义，建筑旁的封闭空地，也指球场

entries.definition: a piece of ground where flowers or vegetables are grown
an enclosed area with buildings inside it
entries.definitionCN: 近义，内有建筑的围起来的院落

normalIntro.en: The old word named a fenced patch of ground, and almost every later sense stays inside that fence.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的老义是围起来的一块地，后来几乎所有的义项都没离开那道篱笆。

normal.en: Yard goes back to a Germanic word for an enclosure, so the fence is part of the meaning.
normal.cn: yard 源自日耳曼语中「围地」的说法，所以篱笆本身就是词义的一部分。

normal.en: Add a word in front and you get a new kind of ground: farmyard, shipyard, brickyard.
normal.cn: 前面加一个词就得到一种新的场地：farmyard、shipyard、brickyard。

normal.en: Yardstick is both a measuring rod and a standard for judging, so the ground word turned into a measure of judgement.
normal.cn: yardstick 既是量尺也是判断的标准，于是一个地面词变成了评判的尺度。

normal.en: The unit of length is written yard, but it came from the same fenced plot, where a measuring stick was kept.
normal.cn: 长度单位写作 yard，但它出自同一块围地，那里放着量长度的木棍。

normal.en: In British English, yard is still the everyday word for a small back garden.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，yard 仍是小后院的日常说法。

abstract.en: Picture a low fence behind a house; everything inside the fence is the yard, whatever you put there.
abstract.cn: 想象屋后一圈矮篱笆，篱笆里的一切都叫 yard，里面放什么都行。

abstract.en: Picture a railway ground packed with tracks: a yard is simply the house yard scaled up to the size of trains.
abstract.cn: 想象铺满铁轨的场地：yard 就是把家宅的院子放大到火车那么大。

abstract.en: Picture a stick leaning by the gate with notches cut in it; that stick is the reason a length is also called a yard.
abstract.cn: 想象门边倚着一根刻了格子的木棍；正因为这根棍，一段长度也叫 yard。

examples.en: My father keeps his old bicycle in the yard behind the house.
examples.cn: 父亲把旧自行车放在屋后的院子里。

examples.en: Trucks waited in line outside the railway yard all night.
examples.cn: 卡车在铁路调车场外排了一整夜。

examples.en: The dress needs two yards of blue cloth.
examples.cn: 这条裙子需要两码蓝布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丫的」——屋后圈着一块空地，孩子在里面跑得满身泥，大人喊一声「丫的，别踩水」，这块院子就是 yard。

root: 日耳曼语词根意为「围起来的一块地」，古英语作 geard，与 garden 同出一源；长度单位 yard 一般认为来自院中固定长度的量尺。

sensesIntro.en: From the fenced home ground, the word widens to working grounds of every kind and narrows to one fixed measure of length.
sensesIntro.cn: 从家宅旁围起的地出发，这个词一方面扩到各类工作场地，另一方面收拢成一个固定的长度单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenced patch of ground beside a building
core.cn: 核心意象：建筑旁边一块被篱笆围起的地

branches.en: The enclosed ground at home stays the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 家宅旁那块围起来的地，是这个词最日常的义项。

branches.en: The same ground given over to work becomes a shipyard or a railway yard.
branches.cn: 同一块地改作干活用，就成了造船场或铁路调车场。

branches.en: A measuring stick kept in the yard gave its length the name yard.
branches.cn: 院子里放着的量尺，把它的长度命名为 yard。

branches.en: Fencing animals in turns the ground into a pen for livestock.
branches.cn: 把动物圈进去，同一块地就变成了牲畜围场。

branches.en: Whatever is fenced and set aside for use shares one image: ground under control.
branches.cn: 凡是圈起来派上用场的地都共享一个意象：被掌控的地。

intro.en: Yard is a free Germanic word that joins with nouns to name particular grounds.
intro.cn: yard 是可以独立使用的日耳曼语词，常与其他名词组合，指特定的场地。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor, so the related forms below are Old French and Germanic relatives rather than Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，下面的相关形式是古法语和日耳曼语亲属词，而不是拉丁词根。

items.example: The children played in the yard.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们在院子里玩。

items.meaning: a measuring rod, also a standard
items.example: Cost is not the only yardstick for success.
items.exampleCN: 成本不是衡量成功的唯一标准。

items.example: Chickens wandered across the farmyard.
items.exampleCN: 鸡在农家庭院里到处走。

items.meaning: a place where ships are built
items.example: Hundreds of workers returned to the shipyard.
items.exampleCN: 数百名工人回到了造船厂。

items.meaning: a place where bricks are made or stored
items.example: The brickyard stood at the edge of the village.
items.exampleCN: 砖厂坐落在村子边上。

items.meaning: ground where trains are sorted and stored
items.example: A long train crept through the railway yard.
items.exampleCN: 一列长火车缓缓穿过调车场。

items.meaning: a paved yard enclosed by walls
items.example: A fountain stood in the middle of the courtyard.
items.exampleCN: 庭院中央立着一座喷泉。

items.example: The bell rang, and the schoolyard emptied.
items.exampleCN: 铃响了，学校操场一下空了。

definition_zh: 打哈欠；哈欠；裂开；令人厌倦的事物
definition_en: to open the mouth wide and breathe in slowly when tired or bored, or the act of doing so
core_image: 开会到一半，有人仰起头，张大嘴，眼睛一起闭上
scene: 会议室里暖气太足，坐在后排的人一个接一个把嘴张得很大又合上。She tried to hide the fact that she was yawning during the lecture.
sceneCN: 这里 yawn 是「打哈欠」（第 1 个义项：疲倦或无聊时张大嘴慢慢吸气）；句意为她努力掩饰自己在听讲座时打哈欠。会议室后排那张得很大的嘴，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 yawn 加 -ing 构成，义为「打哈欠的；裂得很开的」
由 yawn 加 -er 构成，义为「打哈欠的人；乏味的东西」

senses.title: To open the mouth in tiredness
senses.definition: to open the mouth wide and breathe in deeply, usually because one is tired or bored
senses.definitionCN: 因疲倦或无聊而张大嘴深吸一口气
senses.example: She tried to hide the fact that she was yawning during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 她努力掩饰自己在听讲座时打哈欠。
senses.why: The oldest verb meant to open the mouth wide, and tiredness is simply the most common reason for doing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早的意思就是张大嘴，而疲倦只是做这个动作最常见的原因。

senses.title: The open mouth itself
senses.definition: the act or sound of opening the mouth wide and breathing in, taken as a sign of tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 张大嘴吸气这一动作，常被视为疲倦的表现
senses.example: He gave a long yawn before answering the question.
senses.exampleCN: 回答问题前他打了一个长长的哈欠。
senses.why: Any verb of a bodily action can be turned into a noun for that action, so the open mouth becomes a countable thing.
senses.whyCN: 任何表示身体动作的动词都能转成这个动作的名词，于是张嘴这件事变成了可数之物。

senses.title: The ground that opens wide
senses.definition: to open very wide, said of a hole, gap, or space
senses.definitionCN: 指洞口、裂缝或空间张得很大
senses.example: A yawning hole had opened in the road after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，路面上裂开了一个大洞。
senses.why: Because the mouth opens wide when one yawns, the same word is used for any gap that opens just as wide.
senses.whyCN: 打哈欠时嘴张得很开，因此任何同样张得很大的裂口都用这个词。

senses.title: The boring thing
senses.definition: something so dull that it makes people yawn, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 乏味得让人打哈欠的东西，多用于口语
senses.example: The second half of the film was a real yawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的后半段实在无聊。
senses.why: Since yawning signals boredom, the name of the action slides onto the boring thing that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 既然打哈欠表示无聊，这个动作的名字就滑到了引起它的无聊东西身上。

senses.title: The open mouth of an object
senses.definition: a wide opening, as of a cave or a valley, described by the same picture of a gaping mouth
senses.definitionCN: 洞穴或山谷等张开的宽大开口，用同一个「张嘴」的画面来形容
senses.example: The path led into the yawn of the cave.
senses.exampleCN: 小路通进那个张着大口的洞穴。
senses.why: The body picture is projected onto landscape, so a cave mouth is described with the same widening.
senses.whyCN: 身体的画面被投射到景物上，于是洞口也用同一种「张大」来描写。

intro.en: Yawn comes from an Old English verb for opening the mouth wide, and the family is shared with Dutch and German words of similar shape.
intro.cn: yawn 出自古英语中「张大嘴」的动词，与荷兰语、德语中形似的词同属一族。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic verb described the mouth opening, with a long vowel at its centre.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语动词描写张嘴的动作，中间是一个长元音。

items.en: geonian meant to open the mouth wide, and was already used of the tired gesture.
items.cn: 古英语 geonian 意为张大嘴，当时已用于这个疲倦的动作。

items.en: The form shifted toward yane and yonen, and the spelling with w appeared later.
items.cn: 中古英语时期形式变为 yane、yonen，带 w 的拼写后来才出现。

items.en: The spelling settled as yawn, and the noun use followed the verb.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 yawn，名词用法随后从动词衍生出来。

items.en: The picture of a gaping mouth was extended to holes, gaps, and dull things.
items.cn: 张嘴的画面被扩用到洞口、裂缝和乏味的事物上。

note.en: Yawn is easily confused with look-alike words, and sits near a small group of tiredness words.
note.cn: yawn 容易与形近词混淆，也与一小群表示疲倦的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who yawns, or something very boring
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，打哈欠的人，也指极无聊的事物

entries.definition: open very wide, as a gap
entries.definitionCN: 同根形式，张得很大的（如裂口）

entries.definition: an area of short cut grass, spelt almost the same but unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，草坪，词源不同

entries.definition: to extend the arms and body when tired
entries.definitionCN: 相关动作，疲倦时伸展身体

entries.definition: to sleep lightly for a short time
to make someone feel tired and uninterested

normalIntro.en: Yawn is built on the picture of a mouth opening wide, and its relatives all keep that opening.
normalIntro.cn: yawn 建立在张嘴的画面之上，它的同族词也都保留着那个开口。

normal.en: The yawning gap in the road keeps the wide-open mouth of the original gesture.
normal.cn: 路上那个 yawning gap 保留了最初张嘴的宽大开口。

normal.en: Yawner is the person who yawns, and by extension anything so dull it makes you yawn.
normal.cn: yawner 指打哈欠的人，引申为任何无聊到让人打哈欠的东西。

normal.en: Old English geonian already meant to open the mouth, so the tired gesture is the oldest use.
normal.cn: 古英语 geonian 已经是「张嘴」，所以这个疲倦的动作是最早的用法。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so a yawn is both the act and the thing.
normal.cn: 名词与动词拼写相同，所以 yawn 既是动作也是那件事。

normal.en: Yawning is catching: seeing someone yawn often makes you yawn too, which keeps the word in daily talk.
normal.cn: 打哈欠会传染：看到别人打哈欠，自己也常跟着打，这个词因此常在日常话里出现。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting room where one mouth after another opens and closes like small doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一间会议室，一张张嘴像小门一样一个接一个打开又关上。

abstract.en: Picture a cave whose entrance is so wide it looks like a mouth mid-yawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一处洞口宽得像正张着嘴打哈欠。

abstract.en: Picture a dull film where the audience slowly sinks and the screen seems to widen into a black mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一部无聊电影，观众慢慢往下沉，银幕仿佛张成一张黑洞洞的大嘴。

examples.en: She tried to hide the fact that she was yawning during the lecture.
examples.cn: 她努力掩饰自己在听讲座时打哈欠。

examples.en: He gave a long yawn before answering the question.
examples.cn: 回答问题前他打了一个长长的哈欠。

examples.en: A yawning hole had opened in the road after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，路面上裂开了一个大洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哟，嗯」——困得不行时有人仰头张嘴，喉咙里飘出一声「哟，嗯」，这个懒懒的开口动作就是 yawn。

root: 古英语 geonian（张大嘴），属日耳曼语族；与荷兰语 geeuwen、德语 gähnen 同源，词根只表示「张开」。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from a mouth opened wide, the word extends to the gaping openings of the world and to anything boring enough to cause it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张张大的嘴出发，这个词伸向世上各种张开的裂口，也伸向一切无聊到能引起它的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouth opening very wide in tiredness
core.cn: 核心意象：疲倦时张得很大的一张嘴

branches.en: The tired gesture is the oldest and most common sense.
branches.cn: 疲倦时的这个动作是最古老也最常见的义项。

branches.en: The same act becomes a countable noun in daily speech.
branches.cn: 同一个动作在日常话里变成可数的名词。

branches.en: The wide opening is projected onto holes, caves, and valleys.
branches.cn: 张开的形状被投射到洞口、洞穴与山谷上。

branches.en: Boredom is the feeling that causes the gesture, and so names the dull thing.
branches.cn: 无聊是引起这个动作的感受，于是也用它的名字来称乏味之物。

branches.en: One widening movement ties the body and the landscape together.
branches.cn: 同一个张开动作把身体与景物连在了一起。

intro.en: Yawn is a native Germanic word that works as both verb and noun and forms a few adjectives in -ing.
intro.cn: yawn 是本土日耳曼语词，兼作动词和名词，并能加 -ing 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for this word, so the related forms below are its English family, not Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，下面的相关形式是它的英语词族，而不是拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to open the mouth wide when tired
items.example: He yawned twice during the film.
items.exampleCN: 他看电影时打了两次哈欠。

items.meaning: both the act and the thing
items.example: A yawn escaped her before she could stop it.
items.exampleCN: 她还没来得及忍住，就打了个哈欠。

items.meaning: forming the adjective for a wide opening
items.meaningCN: 构成表示张得很开的形容词
items.example: A yawning gap separated the two sides.
items.exampleCN: 双方之间有一条巨大的鸿沟。

items.meaning: one who yawns, or a dull thing
items.meaningCN: 打哈欠的人，或乏味的东西
items.example: The speech was a real yawner.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲真是让人打哈欠。

items.example: The yawning gap in pay worried the workers.
items.exampleCN: 薪酬上的巨大差距让工人们担忧。

items.meaning: to stop a yawn from showing
items.example: She stifled a yawn and kept listening.
items.exampleCN: 她忍住哈欠，继续听下去。

items.meaning: used of behaviour easily copied by others
items.meaningCN: 形容容易被别人跟着做的行为
items.example: Yawning is catching, especially in a warm room.
items.exampleCN: 打哈欠会传染，尤其在暖和的房间里。

items.meaning: to open the mouth wide or stare with it open
items.meaningCN: 相关的动词，张大嘴或张口瞪视
items.example: The crowd gaped at the huge screen.
items.exampleCN: 人群张着嘴盯着巨大的屏幕。

definition_zh: 是；对；嗯（表示同意或应答）
definition_en: an informal word for yes, used to agree, to answer a question, or to show that one is listening
core_image: 电话那头刚说完，这头随口应一声，表示听到了也同意了
scene: 朋友问要不要一起去吃面，另一个人一边拿外套一边随口答应。Yeah, I will be there by seven.
sceneCN: 这里 yeah 是「是；对」（第 1 个义项：口语中表示同意或肯定的应答）；句意为「好，我七点前到」。电话那头随口应一声的样子，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 嗯（表示在听或表示明白）

derivatives.zh: 来自同一源的古旧形式，义为「赞成票；说赞成的人」
yeah 的口语变体，义为「是；对」
yeah 的另一口语变体，义为「是；对」

senses.title: The quick yes
senses.definition: a casual way of saying yes when agreeing to something or answering a question
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事或回答问题时随口说的「是」
senses.example: Yeah, I will be there by seven.
senses.exampleCN: 好，我七点前到。
senses.why: The word is simply yes pronounced loosely in fast speech, so the meaning of yes is kept whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 yes 在快说时松散的发音，所以 yes 的意思完整地保留了下来。

senses.title: The sound of listening
senses.definition: a short sound used to show that one is still listening or has understood
senses.definitionCN: 表示自己仍在听或已经明白的短促应声
senses.example: Yeah, yeah, go on, I am listening.
senses.exampleCN: 嗯，嗯，接着说，我在听。
senses.why: In talk, a quick yes also means that the message arrived, so the same sound becomes a signal of attention.
senses.whyCN: 在对话里，一声「是」也意味着信息收到了，于是同一个声音变成了注意力还在的信号。

senses.title: The doubtful yeah
senses.definition: said with a rising tone to show doubt or disbelief, often in yeah, right
senses.definitionCN: 用升调说出以示怀疑或不相信，常见于 yeah, right
senses.example: Yeah, right, and the bus just flew away.
senses.exampleCN: 是吗，然后公交车就飞走了吧。
senses.why: The same agreement word, said with the wrong tone, turns into its opposite, which is a common joke in English talk.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示同意的小词，用错的语调说出来就变成了反话，这是英语口语里常见的玩笑。

senses.title: The answer to a call
senses.definition: used to answer when someone calls your name or knocks
senses.definitionCN: 别人叫你名字或敲门时的应答
senses.example: Yeah? Come in, the door is open.
senses.exampleCN: 哎？进来吧，门没锁。
senses.why: Answering a call with yes simply confirms that one is present, so the word serves as a doorbell reply.
senses.whyCN: 用「是」来应声，本质上就是确认自己在场，于是这个词成了门铃前的回答。

senses.title: The filler in speech
senses.definition: a long drawn-out yeah used while the speaker thinks, filling a pause in the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 说话人思考时拉长的一声「嗯」，用来填补句子中的停顿
senses.example: Yeah, well, it was not exactly what I meant.
senses.exampleCN: 嗯，这个嘛，那不是我的意思。
senses.why: A word that only signals agreement easily becomes a pause filler, so it can appear without agreeing to anything at all.
senses.whyCN: 一个只表示同意的小词很容易变成填充停顿的声音，于是它可以出现却并不真的同意什么。

intro.en: Yeah is a spoken form of yes, first written down in the nineteenth century to catch the way the word sounds in quick talk.
intro.cn: yeah 是 yes 的口语形式，到十九世纪才被写下来，为的是记下这个词在快说时的声音。

items.en: gēse was one of the emphatic forms of yes, built from the older word for so.
items.cn: 古英语 gēse 是 yes 的强调形式之一，由更古的「如此」一词构成。

items.en: The form reduced toward yes and yis in everyday speech.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，日常口语里逐渐简化为 yes、yis。

items.en: The stressed vowel weakened in informal talk, giving a sound like yeh.
items.cn: 在非正式谈话中重音元音弱化，产生了近似 yeh 的声音。

items.en: Editors began writing yeah in the nineteenth century to record dialogue in fiction.
items.cn: 十九世纪编辑开始用 yeah 记录小说中的对话。

items.en: Yeah is now the ordinary spoken agreement word, while yes stays the written and formal one.
items.cn: 如今 yeah 是口语中平常的同意词，yes 则保留书面与正式的用法。

note.en: Yeah belongs to a small family of spoken agreement words in English.
note.cn: yeah 属于英语口语中表示同意的一小族词。

entries.definition: a short informal yes
entries.definitionCN: 口语变体，简短的一声「是」

entries.definition: another short informal yes
the standard word for agreement
entries.definitionCN: 基础形式，标准的同意词

entries.definition: an informal way of agreeing
a word of agreement or acceptance
used to say that one agrees or has understood
entries.definitionCN: 相关应答，表示同意或明白

normalIntro.en: Yeah is yes worn down by fast speech, and every sense keeps that quick agreement.
normalIntro.cn: yeah 是被快说磨薄了的 yes，各个义项都保留着那声爽快的应承。

normal.en: Take yes and loosen the vowel, and you get yeah, the shape used in conversation.
normal.cn: 把 yes 的元音放松，就得到对话里说的 yeah。

normal.en: The spoken variants yep and yup follow the same pattern of a clipped yes.
normal.cn: 口语变体 yep 与 yup 走的是同一条路子：把 yes 剪短。

normal.en: In yeah, right the rising tone turns the agreement into doubt.
normal.cn: 在 yeah, right 中，升调把同意变成了怀疑。

normal.en: Yeah? said at the door answers a knock without a full sentence.
normal.cn: 在门口说 yeah? 就等于用一个词回应敲门。

normal.en: Fiction writers put yeah in dialogue because it sounds like real speech, which is why it entered print so late.
normal.cn: 小说家把 yeah 写进对话是因为它像真的说话，所以它很晚才进入印刷。

abstract.en: Picture a phone call in which the listener keeps murmuring yeah to show the line is still alive.
abstract.cn: 想象一通电话，听的一方不断低声应 yeah，表示这头还连着火。

abstract.en: Picture two friends nodding fast at the same time, both saying yeah at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两个朋友同时快速点头，一起说出 yeah。

abstract.en: Picture a pause filled with a long drawn yeah while the speaker searches for the right word.
abstract.cn: 想象说话人找词时，用一个拖长的 yeah 把空档填上。

examples.en: Yeah, I will be there by seven.
examples.cn: 好，我七点前到。

examples.en: Yeah, yeah, go on, I am listening.
examples.cn: 嗯，嗯，接着说，我在听。

examples.en: Yeah? Come in, the door is open.
examples.cn: 哎？进来吧，门没锁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耶」——朋友提议去吃面，你一边拿外套一边喊一声「耶」，这一声爽快的答应就是 yeah。

root: yes 的口语弱化形式，源自中古英语 yes，更早为古英语 gēse（强调的「是」）；词根表示「如此、确实」。

sensesIntro.en: One quick agreement becomes a listening sound, a doubtful retort, an answer at the door, and finally a pause filler.
sensesIntro.cn: 一声爽快的同意，先变成表示在听的应声，再变成怀疑的反问、开门的应答，最后成了填充停顿的声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quick yes in conversation
core.cn: 核心意象：对话中一声爽快的「是」

branches.en: The plain agreement is the whole source of the word.
branches.cn: 单纯的同意就是这个词的全部来源。

branches.en: Saying yes often also means the message has been heard.
branches.cn: 说「是」往往也意味着信息已经被听见。

branches.en: The same word with a rising tone says the opposite.
branches.cn: 同一个词用升调说出来就表示相反的意思。

branches.en: Answering a call with yes confirms that someone is there.
branches.cn: 用「是」应答呼唤，就是确认有人在。

branches.en: A word of agreement easily degrades into a filler sound.
branches.cn: 一个表示同意的小词很容易退化成填充声音。

intro.en: Yeah is a word rather than an affix, but it enters fixed phrases that are worth learning as units.
intro.cn: yeah 是词而不是词缀，但它常进入固定说法，适合整块记住。

latinIntro.en: The word is English through and through, with no Latin element, so the related forms below are its spoken relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是地道的英语词，没有拉丁成分，下面的相关形式是它的口语亲属。

items.example: Yeah, that works for me.
items.exampleCN: 行，我这边可以。

items.example: Yeah, right, you ran ten miles.
items.exampleCN: 是吗，你跑了十英里。

items.example: Oh yeah, I forgot to call her.
items.exampleCN: 对了，我忘了给她打电话。

items.example: Yeah, sure, take my umbrella.
items.exampleCN: 行，当然，拿我的伞吧。

items.example: Yep, that is the one I meant.
items.exampleCN: 对，我说的就是那个。

items.example: Yup, it starts at nine.
items.exampleCN: 对，九点开始。

items.meaning: the spoken no that matches yeah
items.meaningCN: 与 yeah 相对的口语「不」
items.example: Nope, not today.
items.exampleCN: 不，今天不行。

items.meaningCN: 表示连声答应或轻微的不耐烦
items.example: Yeah, yeah, I am coming.
items.exampleCN: 好了好了，我来了。

definition_zh: 每年的；一年一次的；每年地；一年一次地
definition_en: happening once every year or calculated over a period of one year
core_image: 同一本台历，每年到同一个月份就翻到同一页
scene: 公司财务把一年的账都收进同一个文件夹，每到年底把同一张表再填一遍。The club holds a yearly meeting in the spring.
sceneCN: 这里 yearly 是「一年一次的」（第 1 个义项：每年发生一次）；句意为俱乐部每年春天开一次会。台历每年翻到同一页，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: yearly 的基础词，义为「年」
由 year 加 long 构成，义为「持续一年的」
与 yearly 意义相近的拉丁来源副词，义为「每年」

senses.title: Once in each cycle
senses.definition: happening once every year, used of events and arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生一次，用于事件与安排
senses.example: The club holds a yearly meeting in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部每年春天开一次会。
senses.why: Adding -ly to year turns the cycle into a repeating schedule, so the word says how often.
senses.whyCN: 给 year 加 -ly，就把这个周期变成了重复的日程，于是词说的是多久一次。

senses.title: Counted over one cycle
senses.definition: calculated over a period of one year, used of pay, income, and reports
senses.definitionCN: 按一年的时长来计算，用于薪酬、收入与报告
senses.example: Her yearly income is enough to cover the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她的年收入足够付房租。
senses.why: If a cycle can be repeated, it can also serve as a unit of counting, so totals are added up by year.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个周期可以重复，它也能充作计数的单位，于是总数按年相加。

senses.title: In each cycle
senses.definition: as an adverb, meaning in every year or once a year
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，意为每年或一年一次
senses.example: The magazine is published yearly.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志每年出版一次。
senses.why: The same form serves as an adverb because -ly marks manner and frequency in English, so no change is needed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式也能作副词，因为 -ly 在英语里既标方式也标频率，不需另加变形。

senses.title: Over the whole of a cycle
senses.definition: covering or lasting for a whole year, said of a period or amount
senses.definitionCN: 持续或涵盖整整一年，用于时段或数量
senses.example: They agreed on a yearly rent for the small shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这家小店谈定了全年租金。
senses.why: A repeating event can also stretch to fill its whole cycle, so the word covers a full year rather than a point in it.
senses.whyCN: 重复发生的事也可以一直铺满整个周期，于是这个词涵盖的是一整年而不是其中的一点。

senses.title: The same as every year
senses.definition: used with verbs to show that something recurs in the same way, as in yearly tradition
senses.definitionCN: 与名词连用时表示情形年年照旧，如 yearly tradition
senses.example: Visiting the old teacher is a yearly tradition for us.
senses.exampleCN: 去看望那位老教师是我们每年的习惯。
senses.why: Since the cycle repeats without change, the word also carries the feeling of a fixed custom.
senses.whyCN: 周期一成不变地重复，于是这个词也带上了固定习俗的意味。

intro.en: Yearly is simply year with the Old English suffix -līc, which became -ly and marked a repeated pattern.
intro.cn: yearly 就是 year 加上古英语后缀 -līc，这个后缀写成 -ly，表示重复的模式。

items.en: gēarlīce was formed from gēar plus the suffix -līce, meaning in the manner of a year.
items.cn: 古英语 gēarlīce 由 gēar 加后缀 -līce 构成，意为「以一年的方式」。

items.en: The suffix reduced to -ly, and year became the first element of a regular adjective.
items.cn: 后缀简化为 -ly，year 成了这个规则形容词的第一个成分。

items.en: The adjective settled alongside the adverb, with the same spelling for both.
items.cn: 形容词与副词并行固定下来，两者拼写相同。

items.en: Yearly was preferred in business and school usage, while annual came in from Latin for formal writing.
items.cn: yearly 多用于商业与学校，正式书面语则用来自拉丁语的 annual。

items.en: Today both forms share the two jobs of describing frequency and counting a full year.
items.cn: 今天这两种形式都兼有表示频率与计算整年的两个用途。

note.en: Yearly is compared with its Latin twin annual and with other frequency words.
note.cn: yearly 常与拉丁来源的 annual 以及表示频率的词对比。

entries.definition: a cycle of about three hundred and sixty-five days
lasting for a whole year
entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词，持续一年的

entries.definition: before the expected time, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，较早，词源不同

entries.definition: happening once a year, from Latin
entries.definitionCN: 近义，拉丁来源的「一年一次的」

entries.definition: happening once a month
entries.definitionCN: 同类频率词，每月一次的

entries.definition: happening every day

normalIntro.en: Yearly shows the everyday English pattern: a time word plus -ly makes a frequency word.
normalIntro.cn: yearly 展示了英语里最常见的构词方式：时间词加 -ly 变成频率词。

normal.en: Swap the base and you get the pattern: month plus -ly is monthly, day plus -ly is daily.
normal.cn: 换掉底词就是同一个模式：month 加 -ly 是 monthly，day 加 -ly 是 daily。

normal.en: The same spelling covers both adjective and adverb, as in yearly report and published yearly.
normal.cn: 同一个拼写兼作形容词和副词，如 yearly report 与 published yearly。

normal.en: Annual does the same job in formal writing, because Latin annus means year.
normal.cn: 正式书面语里 annual 干同样的活，因为拉丁语 annus 就是年。

normal.en: Yearly income is a total gathered over one full cycle, not the money of one moment.
normal.cn: yearly income 是把整个周期加总，而不是某一刻的钱。

normal.en: A yearly tradition borrows the unchanged repetition of the seasons.
normal.cn: yearly tradition 借用了四季一成不变的重复。

abstract.en: Picture a wall calendar whose same page is turned to on the same date every year.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙上的日历，每年同一个日子都翻到同一页。

abstract.en: Picture a folder labelled with one year, filled with exactly one year of bills.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标着年份的文件夹，里面正好装一年的账单。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hand needs a whole year to come back to the same mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个钟，指针要整整一年才回到同一格。

examples.en: The club holds a yearly meeting in the spring.
examples.cn: 俱乐部每年春天开一次会。

examples.en: Her yearly income is enough to cover the rent.
examples.cn: 她的年收入足够付房租。

examples.en: The magazine is published yearly.
examples.cn: 这本杂志每年出版一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一阿里里」——每年结账时票据堆得一「阿里里」，这一年到头的把账算清的活儿，就是 yearly 的每年一次。

root: year（年，古英语 gēar）加后缀 -ly（古英语 -līce，表示以某方式），构成表示频率的形容词与副词。

sensesIntro.en: Turn the cycle into a schedule and the word tells how often, how much, and how long at once.
sensesIntro.cn: 把这个周期变成日程，这个词同时说明了多久一次、多少、以及持续多长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same page of the calendar each year
core.cn: 核心意象：每年翻到日历的同一页

branches.en: A repeated event is the clearest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 重复发生的事件是这个词最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Counting by the cycle turns the word into a unit of total.
branches.cn: 按周期计数，使这个词成为总量的单位。

branches.en: The adverb use states frequency without changing shape.
branches.cn: 副词用法直接说明频率，形式不变。

branches.en: A repeating event can fill its whole cycle, so a full year is covered.
branches.cn: 重复的事可以铺满整个周期，于是涵盖整整一年。

branches.en: Unchanging repetition carries the feeling of custom.
branches.cn: 不变的重复带来习俗的意味。

intro.en: Yearly is built with the productive suffix -ly, which turns time nouns into frequency words.
intro.cn: yearly 由能产后缀 -ly 构成，这个后缀把时间名词变成频率词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for year, annus, gives formal partners such as annual and annually.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「年」的 annus 提供了 annual、annually 等正式对等词。

items.meaning: a cycle of about three hundred and sixty-five days
items.meaningCN: 约三百六十五天的一个周期
items.example: The year ended quietly.
items.exampleCN: 这一年平静地结束了。

items.meaning: forming words such as monthly and daily
items.example: The shop is checked daily.
items.exampleCN: 这家店每天检查。

items.example: They pay rent yearly.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年付房租。

items.example: It was a yearlong project.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个长达一年的项目。

items.example: She gets a monthly report.
items.exampleCN: 她每月收到一份报告。

items.example: The weekly market is on Sunday.
items.exampleCN: 每周的集市在星期日。

items.example: The company reports quarterly.
items.exampleCN: 公司按季度报告。

items.meaning: once a year, in formal style
items.example: The prize is awarded annually.
items.exampleCN: 该奖项每年颁发一次。

definition_zh: 还；仍然；（用于否定）尚未；然而；但是
definition_en: up to now, or still, used mostly in questions and negatives, and also as a word of contrast
core_image: 钟表停在原地，指针还没往前挪，但随时可以挪
scene: 饭桌上菜都摆好了，最后一个人还没到，大家就先把碗筷放下等着。The soup is not ready yet, so please sit down for a moment.
sceneCN: 这里 yet 是「尚未」（第 2 个义项：用在否定句中表示到现在还没发生）；句意为汤还没好，请坐一会儿。钟表停在原地还没往前挪，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 同源方言名词，义为「大门」，与 yet 的副词用法无关
固定说法，义为「到目前为止」

senses.title: Still going on
senses.definition: used to say that something is still true or still continuing at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事到此刻仍然如此或仍在继续
senses.example: There is yet time to change the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 还有时间改计划。
senses.why: The oldest sense meant still or up to now, and that meaning sits inside every later use.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是「仍然、直到现在」，这个意思藏在后来每一种用法里。

senses.title: Not up to now
senses.definition: used in negative sentences or questions to say that something has not happened up to now
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句或疑问句，表示到现在还没发生
senses.example: The soup is not ready yet, so please sit down for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 汤还没好，请坐一会儿。
senses.why: If the word marks the time up to now, then in a negative sentence it marks the point that has not been reached.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词标的是「直到现在」，那么放在否定句里它标的就是尚未到达的那一点。

senses.title: The word of contrast
senses.definition: used as a conjunction to introduce something that contrasts with what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 作连词，引出与上文形成对照的内容
senses.example: The room was small, yet it felt comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 房间很小，然而很舒服。
senses.why: The step from still to however is short: what is still true can quietly contradict what was just claimed.
senses.whyCN: 从「仍然」到「然而」只隔一步：仍然成立的事，可以悄悄推翻刚刚说过的话。

senses.title: One more time
senses.definition: used before again or another to show that something is repeated, often with mild annoyance
senses.definitionCN: 用在 again 或 another 前表示重复，常带一点不耐烦
senses.example: He was late yet again this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早他又一次迟到了。
senses.why: Repetition is just duration continued, so the word of still also marks another round of the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 重复不过是持续下去，所以「仍然」这个词也能标出同样事情又来一轮。

senses.title: The best so far
senses.definition: used after a superlative to mean up to this time
senses.definitionCN: 用在最高级后，表示到现在为止
senses.example: This is her best film yet.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她至今最好的一部电影。
senses.why: Because the word marks the limit of time up to now, a superlative with yet means the record so far.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词标的是时间的上限，所以与最高级连用就表示「到目前为止」的纪录。

intro.en: Yet comes from an Old English word meaning still or up to now, and the conjunction use grew out of that adverb.
intro.cn: yet 出自古英语中意为「仍然、直到现在」的词，连词用法由这个副词长出来。

items.en: The root carried the idea of something continuing up to a point, shared with Dutch and German relatives.
items.cn: 这个词根带有「一直持续到某点」的意思，与荷兰语、德语亲属词共有。

items.en: giet and gīet meant still, or up to this time, in both prose and poetry.
items.cn: 古英语 giet、gīet 在散文与诗歌中都意为「仍然、直到此时」。

items.en: The form shortened to yet, and the negative pattern not yet became common.
items.cn: 形式简化为 yet，否定结构 not yet 变得常用。

items.en: The contrastive use as a conjunction spread in written prose.
items.cn: 作连词表示转折的用法在书面散文中流行起来。

items.en: Uses with comparatives and superlatives settled, giving the best yet and yet again.
items.cn: 与比较级、最高级连用的用法固定下来，产生了 the best yet、yet again。

note.en: Yet is close in spelling to a few short words and in meaning to other time and contrast words.
note.cn: yet 在拼写上接近几个短词，在意思上接近其他时间词与转折词。

entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，日元，词源不同

entries.definition: woven material with holes, or an amount after costs
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，网，净额，词源不同

entries.definition: to obtain or receive, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，得到，词源不同

entries.definition: continuing up to now

used to introduce a contrast

normalIntro.en: Yet marks the time up to now, and every sense either continues that line or turns it into a contrast.
normalIntro.cn: yet 标的是「直到现在」这条线，各个义项要么延续它，要么把它变成转折。

normal.en: Not yet is the most common pattern, because the word lives in the gap before something happens.
normal.cn: not yet 是最常见的搭配，因为这个词就住在事情发生前的空档里。

normal.en: Have yet to do something means the same as have not done it so far.
normal.cn: have yet to do 与「到现在还没做」意思相同。

normal.en: As yet means up to this point, and it keeps the pure time meaning.
normal.cn: as yet 意为「到目前为止」，保留了纯粹的时间义。

normal.en: In the sentence the room was small, yet comfortable, the word simply turns the line back.
normal.cn: 在「房间小，然而舒服」这句里，这个词只是把话拐了一个弯。

normal.en: Yet again repeats an event, so the time word doubles as a word of annoyance.
normal.cn: yet again 重复同一件事，于是时间词兼作不耐烦的语气词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a clock that has not moved, though the minute could turn at any second.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按着钟面，指针还没动，可随时会转。

abstract.en: Picture a table set for dinner with one chair still empty.
abstract.cn: 想象晚饭的桌子摆好了，只有一张椅子还空着。

abstract.en: Picture a straight road that bends once at the end: still, then a quiet contrast.
abstract.cn: 想象一条直路在末尾拐了一下：本是一直往前，忽然有个转折。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耶，特」——等公交等了很久，车还没来，旁边有人喊「耶，特慢」，这「还没来、仍然在等」的状态就是 yet。

root: 古英语 giet（仍然、直到此时），属日耳曼语族；由「持续到某点」的词根发展出转折与重复两种用法。

sensesIntro.en: One time line up to now splits into still, not yet, one more time, and the best so far, and then bends into however.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条「直到现在」的时间线先分出「仍然」「尚未」「又一次」「至今最好」，最后拐成「然而」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the clock has not moved yet
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表的指针还没往前挪

branches.en: Continued truth up to now is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 到此刻仍然成立，是最古老的义项。

branches.en: The same line in a negative sentence marks what has not happened.
branches.cn: 同一条线放进否定句，就标出尚未发生的事。

branches.en: Repetition and records are both measured on the same line.
branches.cn: 重复与纪录都在这同一条线上量。

branches.en: From time the word slides to contrast, ending a claim and turning it.
branches.cn: 这个词从时间滑向转折，结束一个说法再把它拐弯。

branches.en: A short word covering both duration and contrast shows how one root can bend.
branches.cn: 一个短词兼管持续与转折，说明一个词根可以怎样弯折。

intro.en: Yet works alone as adverb and conjunction, and appears in a few fixed phrases worth learning whole.
intro.cn: yet 单独作副词和连词，也出现在几个值得整块记住的固定说法里。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for the word; Latin marked the same idea with adhuc and tamen.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语用 adhuc 与 tamen 表达同样的意思。

items.example: I have not decided yet.
items.exampleCN: 我还没决定。

items.example: It was cheap, yet useful.
items.exampleCN: 它很便宜，却很有用。

items.example: The train has not yet arrived.
items.exampleCN: 火车还没到。

items.example: They have yet to reply.
items.exampleCN: 他们尚未回复。

items.example: As yet there is no news.
items.exampleCN: 目前还没有消息。

items.example: He forgot the key yet again.
items.exampleCN: 他又一次忘了带钥匙。

items.example: That was his quickest run yet.
items.exampleCN: 那是他至今跑得最快的一次。

items.example: Latin adhuc means up to this point.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 adhuc 意为「到此刻为止」。

definition_en: a young person, especially a boy or girl between childhood and adult life
core_image: 巷子里骑着车飞过的那个半大孩子，衣服还短一截
scene: 傍晚巷口一群半大孩子在追球，喊声一直传到楼上。A few youngsters were playing football in the school yard after class.
sceneCN: 这里 youngster 是「年轻人；孩子」（第 1 个义项：介于童年与成年之间的年轻人）；句意为放学后几个孩子在操场踢球。巷子里骑车飞过的半大孩子，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 一个前途看好的年轻人

derivatives.zh: youngster 的基础词，义为「年轻的」
同根名词，义为「青春；青年人」

senses.title: The young person
senses.definition: a young person, used especially of children and teenagers in an informal tone
senses.definitionCN: 年轻的人，尤指儿童与十几岁的少年，语气随意
senses.example: A few youngsters were playing football in the school yard after class.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后几个孩子在操场踢球。
senses.why: The suffix -ster once marked a person, so young plus -ster simply means the one who is young.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ster 过去用来标人，所以 young 加 -ster 就是「年轻的那个人」。

senses.title: The young lad
senses.definition: a boy or young man, often said with warmth or a touch of familiarity
senses.definitionCN: 男孩子或年轻男子，常带亲切或熟稔的语气
senses.example: The youngster at the counter helped me find the right ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台后的小伙子帮我找到了对的车票。
senses.why: Because the word names a person rather than a stage, it fits friendly address as easily as description.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词称的是人而不是阶段，所以既能客观描述也能亲切称呼。

senses.title: The young animal
senses.definition: a young animal, used in farming and in writing about wildlife
senses.definitionCN: 年幼的动物，用于农事与描写野生动物的文字
senses.example: The keeper fed the youngsters before the park opened.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养员在公园开门前先喂了那些幼崽。
senses.why: The word for a young person is extended to animals whenever the writer wants a warm tone.
senses.whyCN: 只要作者想要温暖的语气，用来指年轻人的词就会延伸到动物身上。

senses.title: The member of the team
senses.definition: a young member of a team or group, often contrasted with the experienced ones
senses.definitionCN: 队伍或团体中年轻的一员，常与老队员对照
senses.example: Two youngsters in the squad scored in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 队里两名年轻球员在下半场进了球。
senses.why: In a group of mixed ages, the word picks out the younger ones, so it becomes a role as well as a stage.
senses.whyCN: 在年龄混合的群体里，这个词挑出较年轻的那些，于是它既是阶段也是角色。

senses.title: The person of little experience
senses.definition: a person new to a job or trade, used with a hint of judgement
senses.definitionCN: 刚进入某行业或工作的人，带一点评判意味
senses.example: He was still a youngster in the trade and asked many questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这行还算新手，问了很多问题。
senses.why: Youth stands for inexperience as well as for age, so the word can weigh someone in a profession too.
senses.whyCN: 年轻不仅指年龄也指经验少，所以这个词也能用来衡量一个人在行业里的分量。

intro.en: Youngster is young plus the old suffix -ster, which once named the person who did or was something.
intro.cn: youngster 是 young 加上古老后缀 -ster，这个后缀过去用来指做某事或具有某特征的人。

items.en: The suffix -estre named a woman of a trade or role, as in bæcestre, a baker.
items.cn: 后缀 -estre 用来指从事某行业或角色的女性，如 bæcestre 即女面包师。

items.en: The suffix reduced to -ster and spread to male agents and to people of a kind.
items.cn: 后缀简化为 -ster，扩用到男性施动者以及某类人身上。

items.en: Youngster appeared in the sixteenth century as a plain word for a young person.
items.cn: youngster 于十六世纪出现，是「年轻人」的普通说法。

items.en: The word spread to animals and to team members in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词扩用到动物与队伍成员上。

items.en: Today it is mostly informal, and youth remains the neutral noun.
items.cn: 今天它多为口语，中性的名词仍是 youth。

note.en: Youngster sits among several words that name young people with different tones.
note.cn: youngster 处在几个语气不同、都指年轻人的词之间。

normalIntro.en: The suffix -ster turns a quality into a person, and youngster is a clean example.
normalIntro.cn: 后缀 -ster 把性质变成人，youngster 就是一个干净的例子。

normal.en: Compare trickster: trick plus -ster gives a person who tricks, so young plus -ster gives one who is young.
normal.cn: 对照 trickster：trick 加 -ster 是会耍花招的人，所以 young 加 -ster 就是年轻的人。

normal.en: The suffix began in Old English as -estre and named women in trades, then widened to all people.
normal.cn: 这个后缀在古英语作 -estre，指从业的女性，后来扩到所有人。

normal.en: The plural is simply youngsters, so the word behaves like any regular noun.
normal.cn: 复数就是 youngsters，和普通名词一样。

normal.en: Youth is the neutral noun, while youngster is warmer and more spoken.
normal.cn: youth 是中性的名词，youngster 更温暖也更口语。

normal.en: In sport writing, youngsters often means the young players on a team rather than children.
normal.cn: 在体育报道里，youngsters 常指队里的年轻球员，而不是小孩。

abstract.cn: 想象一个男孩骑车太快地拐过街角，袖子短了一截。

abstract.en: Picture a group of small figures chasing a ball until the light goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一群小身影追着球，一直追到天黑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「羊子的」——山坡上一群小羊蹦来蹦去，那就是羊崽子，跟说「那帮年轻的」一个口气，于是 youngster 指年轻人。

root: young（年轻，古英语 geong）加后缀 -ster（古英语 -estre，指从事某事或具有某特征的人）。

sensesIntro.en: One quality turned into a person easily spreads from children to a friendly lad, to animals, to team members, and to the inexperienced.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个变成人的性质，很容易从孩子扩到亲切的小伙子、动物、队里的队员，以及经验少的人。

core.cn: 核心意象：一个半大孩子匆匆跑过

branches.en: A young person is the plain, original sense.
branches.cn: 年轻人是这个词朴素的本义。

branches.en: Personhood rather than age lets the word serve as warm address.
branches.cn: 称的是人而不是年龄，所以它能用作亲切的称呼。

branches.en: The warm tone carries over to young animals.
branches.cn: 温暖的语气延伸到了动物的幼崽。

branches.en: In a mixed group, the word picks out the younger members.
branches.cn: 在年龄混合的群体里，这个词挑出较年轻的成员。

branches.en: Youth also means inexperience, which gives the word a judging edge.
branches.cn: 年轻也意味着经验少，于是这个词带上评判色彩。

intro.cn: youngster 由 -ster 构成，这个后缀造施动名词已有一千多年。

latinIntro.en: Latin made similar age words with -anus and with iuvenis; English kept its own -ster instead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 -anus 和 iuvenis 造类似的年龄词，英语则保留了自己的 -ster。

items.example: Youth is no excuse for rudeness.
