definition_zh: 你自己；你亲自；你的正常状态
definition_en: the reflexive form of you, used when the person spoken to is both the doer and the receiver of an action
core_image: 一个人照镜子，镜里镜外都是他自己
scene: 朋友第一次独自做饭，发来一张焦黑的锅底照片。You need to be patient while learning the whole routine.
sceneCN: 这里 yourself 是「你自己」（第 1 个义项：反身代词，动作的执行者与承受者是同一个人）；句意为学做饭时要对自己有耐心。一个人照镜子，镜里镜外都是自己，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 你亲自；你本人（强调用法）
你的正常状态；你的常态

derivatives.zh: yourself 的复数形式，义为「你们自己」
yourself 的后一成分，义为「自我；自身」
由 self 加 -ish 构成，义为「自私的」，与 yourself 同一词根

senses.title: The same person as doer and receiver
senses.definition: used when the listener does something to or for the same person, so doer and receiver are one
senses.definitionCN: 听话者对自己做某事或为自己做某事，执行者与承受者合为一人
senses.example: You should give yourself more time to learn the new job.
senses.exampleCN: 你该给自己更多时间熟悉新工作。
senses.why: Self is added to the possessive so the pronoun can point back at its own subject, which is what a reflexive needs.
senses.whyCN: 把 self 加到所有格后，代词才能指回自己的主语，这正是反身代词所需的。

senses.title: The person in emphasis
senses.definition: used after a noun or at the end of a clause to stress that it was really the listener
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后或句末，强调确实是听话者本人
senses.example: You yourself said the plan would never work.
senses.exampleCN: 你自己说过这个计划行不通。
senses.why: Repeating the pronoun as self makes the reference impossible to miss, so it becomes a way of stressing.
senses.whyCN: 把代词以 self 的形式重说一遍，指谁就绝不含糊，于是成了强调手段。

senses.title: The natural state
senses.definition: used after be or feel to mean one's normal healthy or usual condition
senses.definitionCN: 用在 be 或 feel 之后，指正常、健康或平时的状态
senses.example: You have not been yourself since the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家以后你就不太对劲了。
senses.why: If the self is the whole person, then being away from it is being unlike one's normal state.
senses.whyCN: 如果 self 指整个人，那么离开它就是不在平常的状态。

senses.title: The person acting alone
senses.definition: used after by to mean without help from anyone else
senses.definitionCN: 用在 by 之后，表示没有别人帮忙
senses.example: Can you carry both boxes by yourself?
senses.exampleCN: 你一个人能搬这两个箱子吗？
senses.why: Since the reflexive sends the action back to one person, adding by excludes everyone else.
senses.whyCN: 既然反身代词把动作收回到一个人身上，加上 by 就把其他人都排除在外。

senses.title: The person as one of a group
senses.definition: used instead of yourselves when the listener is addressed as one of a group rather than all together
senses.definitionCN: 当听话者代表一群人中的一位、而非整群人一起时，用它代替 yourselves
senses.example: Each of you should introduce yourself before we start.
senses.exampleCN: 开始之前，你们每个人都要介绍一下自己。
senses.why: English divides between one listener and a whole audience inside the same pronoun, so the reflexive has to choose its form.
senses.whyCN: 英语在同一个代词里兼指一个人和整群听众，于是反身形式必须作选择。

intro.en: Yourself joins your, the possessive of you, with self, a word meaning one's own person.
intro.cn: yourself 由 you 的所有格 your 与意为「本人」的 self 组合而成。

items.en: self was an adjective meaning the same or very, and could follow a pronoun to strengthen it.
items.cn: 古英语 self 是形容词，意为「同一的、正是的」，跟在代词后起加强作用。

items.en: Combinations such as þe selfum appear in prose, though the modern shape came later.
items.cn: 古英语散文里已见 þe selfum 之类组合，现代形式则出现较晚。

items.en: The modern pattern of pronoun plus self formed, with yourself and himself among the first.
items.cn: 代词加 self 的现代模式形成，yourself 与 himself 属于最早的一批。

items.en: The reflexive and the emphatic uses settled, and the by yourself pattern became everyday.
items.cn: 反身用法与强调用法固定，by yourself 也成了日常说法。

items.en: The plural yourselves was kept for groups, so the two forms divide the work.
items.cn: 复数 yourselves 保留给群体使用，两种形式就此分工。

note.en: Yourself is compared with the other pronouns ending in -self and with related reflexives.
note.cn: yourself 与其它以 -self 结尾的代词以及相关反身形式作对照。

entries.definition: the reflexive for a group of listeners
belonging to the listener
a person's own being
the reflexive for the speaker
the reflexive for a male third person
the reflexive for anyone, in formal style
entries.definitionCN: 正式对等形式，一个人自己

normalIntro.en: The pattern is simple: possessive plus self, and the possessive shows whose self it is.
normalIntro.cn: 模式很简单：所有格加 self，所有格说明是谁的自己。

normal.en: Your is the possessive, so yourself literally marks the self that belongs to you.
normal.cn: your 是所有格，所以 yourself 字面上就是属于你的那个自己。

normal.en: Swap the possessive and the whole set appears: myself, himself, herself, ourselves.
normal.cn: 换掉所有格，整套词就出来了：myself、himself、herself、ourselves。

normal.en: The plural is irregular in its first half but regular in its second: yourselves.
normal.cn: 复数前半不规则，后半规则：yourselves。

normal.en: By yourself means alone, because a reflexive pushes the action back to one person.
normal.cn: by yourself 意为独自，因为反身代词把动作收回一个人身上。

normal.en: Self began as an adjective meaning very, which explains how the pronoun became emphatic.
normal.cn: self 原是意为「正是」的形容词，这解释了代词为何变得强调。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror where the person outside and the person inside are doing the same thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，镜外的人和镜里的人做着同一件事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing back at its own chest instead of at someone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不指别人，而是指回自己的胸口。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair at a family meal where one person has been unlike himself all evening.
abstract.cn: 想象家宴上一张空椅，那个人整晚都不像平时的自己。

examples.en: You should give yourself more time to learn the new job.
examples.cn: 你该给自己更多时间熟悉新工作。

examples.en: You yourself said the plan would never work.
examples.cn: 你自己说过这个计划行不通。

examples.en: Can you carry both boxes by yourself?
examples.cn: 你一个人能搬这两个箱子吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有谁儿媳妇」——照镜子时自问「有谁儿媳妇比我还操心」，镜子里那位就是你自己，于是 yourself 指你自己。

root: your（you 的所有格，古英语 ēower）加 self（古英语 self，意为「本人、正是」），构成反身代词。

sensesIntro.en: A pronoun that points back at its own subject becomes reflexivity, emphasis, a sense of normal state, and a way to say alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个指回自身主语的代词，长出了反身、强调、常态与「独自」几种用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror that shows the same person twice
core.cn: 核心意象：镜里镜外是同一个人的镜子

branches.en: Sending the action back to the doer is the core use.
branches.cn: 把动作送回执行者，是核心用法。

branches.en: Repeating the reference makes it emphatic.
branches.cn: 把指称再说一遍，就成了强调。

branches.en: Being away from the self means being unlike one's normal state.
branches.cn: 离开自己，就是不在平常的状态。

branches.en: With by, the reflexive shuts everyone else out.
branches.cn: 配上 by，反身代词就把别人都关在门外。

branches.en: Addressed to individuals within a group, the singular form is chosen.
branches.cn: 对群体中逐位说话时，选单数形式。

intro.en: Yourself is a compound of a possessive and self, and the -self family works as a pattern.
intro.cn: yourself 是所有格与 self 的复合词，-self 这一族按同一模式构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin used the pronoun se for the reflexive, and that element survives in English in words such as suicide and separate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用代词 se 表反身，这个成分以 suicide、separate 等词残留在英语中。

items.example: Be kind to yourself.
items.exampleCN: 对自己好一点。

items.example: Look after yourselves.
items.exampleCN: 你们照顾好自己。

items.example: I taught myself to swim.
items.exampleCN: 我自学游泳。

items.example: He cut himself shaving.
items.exampleCN: 他刮胡子时刮伤了自己。

items.example: One should not praise oneself too much.
items.exampleCN: 人不应过分夸自己。

items.example: The self is not fixed.
items.exampleCN: 自我不是固定不变的。

items.example: Latin se appears in secede and seduce.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 se 出现在 secede 与 seduce 中。

items.example: She finished it by herself.
items.exampleCN: 她一个人完成了。

definition_zh: 青春；青年时期；年轻人；少年
definition_en: the period of life when one is young, or young people as a group
core_image: 操场上刚跑完一圈的脸，汗亮着，喘着还要再跑
scene: 校门口的公交车一停，背书包的人一下涌下来，站台立刻热闹起来。He spent his youth working in his father's shop.
sceneCN: 这里 youth 是「青年时期」（第 2 个义项：年轻时的那段人生阶段）；句意为他年轻时在父亲的店里干活。操场上一张张刚跑完还喘着的脸，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 youth 加 -ful 构成，义为「年轻的；有朝气的」
同一词根的形容词，义为「年轻的」
由 youthful 加 -ly 构成，义为「年轻地」

senses.title: The state of being young
senses.definition: the quality or state of being young, seen as a stage of strength and change
senses.definitionCN: 年轻这一性质或状态，被视为有力气、爱变化的阶段
senses.example: The first grey hairs made him think about his lost youth.
senses.exampleCN: 第一根白发让他想起了逝去的青春。
senses.why: The noun came from the adjective for young, so it names the condition rather than a person at first.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自表示年轻的形容词，所以它先指状态而不是某个人。

senses.title: The early period of life
senses.definition: the time of life between childhood and adult life, treated as a fixed period
senses.definitionCN: 童年与成年之间的那段时间，作为一个人生阶段
senses.example: He spent his youth working in his father's shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他年轻时在父亲的店里干活。
senses.why: Once the condition is bounded in time, it becomes a stage with a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个状态被划出时间范围，它就变成了有始有终的一个阶段。

senses.title: The young people
senses.definition: young people taken together as one group in society
senses.definitionCN: 社会上作为一个整体的年轻人
senses.example: The club was built for the youth of the neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部是为附近的年轻人建的。
senses.why: A name for a quality easily slides onto the people who have it, so the stage becomes the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 表示性质的名词很容易滑到具有这种性质的人身上，于是阶段变成了人群。

senses.title: The individual lad
senses.definition: a young man, usually a teenager, in reports and police language
senses.definitionCN: 年轻男子，通常指十几岁的，多用于报道与警方说法
senses.example: Two youths were seen running from the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 有人看见两个少年从大门口跑出去。
senses.why: The group word slips back to a single member, which is why the plural youths names individuals.
senses.whyCN: 群体词又滑回单个成员，所以复数 youths 指的是一个个少年。

senses.title: The early stage of anything
senses.definition: the early period of an institution, art form, or movement
senses.definitionCN: 机构、艺术形式或运动的早期阶段
senses.example: The idea was formed in the youth of the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法形成于互联网的早期。
senses.why: Since the word marks early life, any growing thing can borrow it for its own early years.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指生命的早期，任何成长中的事物都能借它来说自己的早年。

intro.en: Youth comes from an Old English noun geoguþ, built on the same root as the adjective young.
intro.cn: youth 出自古英语名词 geoguþ，与形容词 young 同根。

items.en: The root supplied both an adjective for being young and a noun for the age of youth.
items.cn: 这个词根同时提供了表示年轻的形容词与表示青年期的名词。

items.en: geoguþ named the period of young age and also the young people of a place.
items.cn: 古英语 geoguþ 既指青年时期，也指一个地方的年轻人。

items.en: The form became youthe and then youth, with the th kept as a sign of the noun.
items.cn: 形式先为 youthe，后为 youth，保留 th 作为名词的标记。

items.en: The word spread to institutions and movements in their early stages.
items.cn: 这个词扩用到处于早期阶段的机构与运动上。

items.en: The plural youths settled for individual young men, especially in reports.
items.cn: 复数 youths 固定指一个个年轻男子，尤其见于报道。

note.en: Youth is compared with its own family and with words for the same stage of life.
note.cn: youth 与自己的词族以及表示同一人生阶段的词作对照。

entries.definition: having the qualities of youth
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，有朝气的，年轻的

entries.definition: not old
young men, one by one
the stage between childhood and adulthood
the length of time one has lived
the last stage of life

normalIntro.en: One root gives young, youth, and youthful, all pointing at the same stage of life.
normalIntro.cn: 一个词根给出 young、youth、youthful，都指向人生的同一阶段。

normal.en: Youthful adds -ful, meaning full of youth, and is used of looks and energy.
normal.cn: youthful 加 -ful，意为充满青春，用于外貌与精力。

normal.en: The noun keeps a th sound while the adjective keeps a ng sound, a common Old English pair.
normal.cn: 名词保留 th 音，形容词保留 ng 音，这是古英语常见的一对。

normal.en: The youth of a place can mean its young people, as in the youth of the neighbourhood.
normal.cn: the youth of a place 可以指当地的年轻人。

normal.en: Germans call young people die Jugend, a close cousin of the same root.
normal.cn: 德语称年轻人为 die Jugend，是同一词根的近亲。

normal.en: In news reports, a youth is one young man, which is why youths is plural.
normal.cn: 新闻里 a youth 指一个年轻男子，所以复数是 youths。

abstract.en: Picture a track after a race, faces red and shining, still wanting another lap.
abstract.cn: 想象跑完一圈的跑道，一张张脸红亮着，还想再跑一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a school gate that opens and pours out a wave of bags and voices.
abstract.cn: 想象校门一开，涌出一片书包和喊声。

abstract.en: Picture a museum wall of early drawings from a young art form.
abstract.cn: 想象一面展墙，挂着某门年轻艺术的早期作品。

examples.en: He spent his youth working in his father's shop.
examples.cn: 他年轻时在父亲的店里干活。

examples.en: The club was built for the youth of the neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 这个俱乐部是为附近的年轻人建的。

examples.en: Two youths were seen running from the gate.
examples.cn: 有人看见两个少年从大门口跑出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「犹思」——上了年纪的人夜里「犹思」当年跑操场的日子，那段还想再来一遍的岁月就是 youth。

root: 古英语 geoguþ，与形容词 geong（年轻）同根，属日耳曼语族，与德语 Jugend 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A name for the state of being young becomes a stage of life, then a whole generation, then one lad, and finally the early years of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示年轻状态的名词，先变成人生阶段，再变成一代人、一个少年，最后成为任何事物的早年。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fresh faces still ready to run again
core.cn: 核心意象：还想着再跑一圈的年轻面孔

branches.en: The condition of being young is where the noun began.
branches.cn: 年轻的状态是这个名词的起点。

branches.en: Bounded in time, the condition becomes a stage.
branches.cn: 划出时间范围后，状态成了一个阶段。

branches.en: The quality passes to the people who have it.
branches.cn: 性质转移到了拥有它的人身上。

branches.en: From the group the word narrows back to one young man.
branches.cn: 从群体又收窄到单个年轻男子。

branches.en: Anything growing can borrow the word for its early years.
branches.cn: 任何成长中的事物都能借它说自己的早年。

intro.en: Youth forms youthful with -ful, and the same root also gives the adjective young.
intro.cn: youth 加 -ful 构成 youthful，同一词根还给出形容词 young。

latinIntro.en: Latin used iuventus for youth, which appears in English in juvenile and rejuvenate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 iuventus 表示青春，它出现在 juvenile 与 rejuvenate 等英语词里。

items.example: The youth of the town meet here.
items.exampleCN: 镇上的年轻人在这里聚会。

items.example: She still has a youthful voice.
items.exampleCN: 她的声音还透着年轻。

items.example: He dressed youthfully.
items.exampleCN: 他穿得很年轻。

items.example: A young bird left the nest.
items.exampleCN: 一只小鸟离了巢。

items.meaning: a place for young people to meet
items.example: The youth club opens at four.
items.exampleCN: 青年俱乐部四点开门。

items.example: Latin iuventus gives juvenile.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 iuventus 给出 juvenile。

items.example: Latin iuvenis is behind juvenile.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 iuvenis 是 juvenile 的来源。

items.example: The holiday rejuvenated her.
items.exampleCN: 这个假期让她重新有了活力。

definition_zh: 零；零度；无；微不足道的人
definition_en: the number that comes before one, the point marked zero on a scale, or nothing at all
core_image: 温度计上那条细细的刻度线，左边是负数，右边是正数
scene: 夜里降温，院子里的水盆结了一层薄冰，气温表停在最低那道线上。The temperature fell to zero just after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 zero 是「零度」（第 2 个义项：刻度上的零点）；句意为刚过午夜气温就降到了零度。温度计上那条细细的刻度线，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: zero 的另一种复数形式，义为「零；若干个零」
由 zero 加 -th 构成，义为「第零的（序列中的第一个）」

senses.title: The number before one
senses.definition: the number that comes before one, written as 0, and used to show that there is none of something
senses.definitionCN: 排在 1 之前的数，写作 0，用来表示某物一点也没有
senses.example: Write a zero at the end of the number and the value grows ten times.
senses.exampleCN: 在数字末尾添一个零，数值就扩大十倍。
senses.why: The word came from Arabic through Italian, where it named the empty place in a written number.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经意大利语来自阿拉伯语，在那里它指数字书写中空出来的那一位。

senses.title: The mark on a scale
senses.definition: the point marked zero on a scale of temperature or measurement, from which values go up or down
senses.definitionCN: 温度或测量刻度上的零点，数值由此向上或向下
senses.example: The temperature fell to zero just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 刚过午夜气温就降到了零度。
senses.why: A number that means nothing becomes a useful fixed point, so scales borrow it as their starting line.
senses.whyCN: 一个表示「无」的数成了好用的固定点，于是各种刻度都借它当起始线。

senses.title: Nothing at all
senses.definition: used as an adjective or noun to mean no amount whatever, as in zero chance
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词或名词，表示一点也没有，如 zero chance
senses.example: There is zero chance of rain before evening.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚前下雨的可能性为零。
senses.why: Since zero states the absence of amount, it fits any noun where none of something exists.
senses.whyCN: 既然零表示数量的空缺，它就能配任何「一点也没有」的名词。

senses.title: The person of no importance
senses.definition: an unimportant or unsuccessful person, used in informal speech as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 不重要或没成就的人，口语中用作贬称
senses.example: He called himself a zero after losing the match.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉比赛后他自称是个废物。
senses.why: If zero means nothing, then a person worth nothing is called a zero by the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 既然零意味着什么都不是，按同样的逻辑，毫无价值的人就被叫作零。

senses.title: The starting point
senses.definition: the lowest or first point from which something is counted or measured
senses.definitionCN: 计数或测量所依据的最低点或最初点
senses.example: They had to build the whole system from zero.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不得不从零开始搭整套系统。
senses.why: A line value everyone shares becomes a place to start, so zero also names a beginning.
senses.whyCN: 一条人人共有的数值线就成了起点，于是零也指开端。

intro.en: Zero came into English through Italian and French from Arabic ṣifr, which first meant empty.
intro.cn: zero 经意大利语与法语进入英语，源自阿拉伯语 ṣifr，最初意为「空的」。

items.en: ṣifr meant empty and was used for the empty place in a written numeral.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 ṣifr 意为「空的」，用来指数字书写中空出来的那一位。

items.en: Scholars translated the Arabic word as zephirum or cifra, and the empty place became a sign.
items.cn: 学者把阿拉伯语译作 zephirum 或 cifra，那个空位成了一个符号。

items.en: zefiro and zero named both the sign and the number it stood for.
items.cn: 意大利语 zefiro 与 zero 既指标记也指它所代表的数。

items.en: The form passed into French as zéro before reaching English.
items.cn: 这一形式先成为法语 zéro，再进入英语。

items.en: English took zero in the seventeenth century, and it later spread to temperature scales and figures of speech.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 zero，后来扩用到温度刻度与各种说法中。

note.en: Zero is compared with the other words for nothing and with the number words around it.
note.cn: zero 与其它表示「无」的词以及相邻的数词作对照。

entries.definition: a code or a written figure, from the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一阿拉伯语来源，密码，数字

entries.definition: a soft gentle wind, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，和风，词源不同

entries.definition: the ordinal form, as in zeroth law
entries.definitionCN: 同根序数词，如 zeroth law

entries.definition: no thing at all
zero, used in scores and records
entries.definitionCN: 近义，比分与记录里的零

entries.definition: the number after zero

normalIntro.en: The word travelled from an Arabic word for empty into English, keeping the idea of a gap.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从阿拉伯语中表示「空」的词一路走进英语，保留了空位的观念。

normal.en: Write a zero after a number and you fill a place that adds a power of ten.
normal.cn: 在数后添零就是占了空位，却把数值提高十倍。

normal.en: Its cousin cipher keeps the old meaning of a written sign as well as a code.
normal.cn: 同源的 cipher 既保留「书写符号」也指密码。

normal.en: Zero tolerance and zero chance show the adjective use meaning none at all.
normal.cn: zero tolerance 与 zero chance 显示了「毫无」的形容用法。

normal.en: Below zero and zero degrees belong to the temperature scale, the fixed point of measuring.
normal.cn: below zero 与 zero degrees 属于温度刻度，是测量的固定点。

normal.en: The plural can be zeros or zeroes, and both appear in print.
normal.cn: 复数可写 zeros 或 zeroes，两种都在书面上出现。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line on a thermometer with ice on one side and steam on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计上一条细线，一边是冰，一边是蒸汽。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair in a classroom where a pupil should be sitting.
abstract.cn: 想象教室里本该坐人的一张空椅。

abstract.en: Picture a row of digits with one empty slot glowing in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一排数字，中间有一格空位发着光。

examples.en: The temperature fell to zero just after midnight.
examples.cn: 刚过午夜气温就降到了零度。

examples.en: There is zero chance of rain before evening.
examples.cn: 傍晚前下雨的可能性为零。

examples.en: They had to build the whole system from zero.
examples.cn: 他们不得不从零开始搭整套系统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「走喽」——跑完最后一圈记分牌上只剩一个圆圈，人也「走喽」，场上什么也不剩，这个圆圈就是 zero。

root: 经意大利语、法语借自阿拉伯语 ṣifr（空的、空位），中世纪拉丁语作 zephirum、cifra；与 cipher 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The sign for an empty place becomes a number, then a fixed point on scales, a total absence, and a word for someone worth nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示空位的符号先成为数字，再成为刻度上的固定点、彻底的「无」，最后指毫无价值的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the line on a scale where nothing is counted
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度上什么都不计的那条线

branches.en: The number grew out of a written gap for an empty place.
branches.cn: 数字是从书写中表示空位的空格长出来的。

branches.en: Scales take that number as a fixed reference line.
branches.cn: 各种刻度把这个数当作固定参照线。

branches.en: Saying nobody has any of something uses the same zero.
branches.cn: 说某人毫无某物也用同一个零。

branches.en: A person worth nothing is called by the number that means nothing.
branches.cn: 毫无价值的人就用表示「无」的数来称。

branches.en: The shared line also becomes the place to begin.
branches.cn: 这条共有的线也成了开始的起点。

intro.en: Zero forms a regular plural and a rare ordinal, and appears in many fixed phrases.
intro.cn: zero 有规则的复数与少见的序数形式，并出现在许多固定说法中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form cifra, taken from Arabic, is the ancestor of both zero and cipher.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 cifra 借自阿拉伯语，既是 zero 也是 cipher 的祖先。

items.example: Count down from zero.
items.exampleCN: 从零开始倒数。

items.example: Add two zeros to the figure.
items.exampleCN: 在这个数字后加两个零。

items.meaning: forming zeroes, used in British style
items.example: The dial shows three zeroes.
items.exampleCN: 表盘上显示三个零。

items.example: The zeroth law comes before the first.
items.exampleCN: 第零定律排在第一条之前。

items.example: Latin cifra gives both zero and cipher.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cifra 同时给出 zero 与 cipher。

items.example: Arabic sifr passed into many languages.
items.exampleCN: 阿拉伯语 sifr 流入许多语言。

items.example: It stayed below zero all week.
items.exampleCN: 整周都在零下。

items.meaning: no acceptance of an offence at all
items.example: The school has zero tolerance for cheating.
items.exampleCN: 学校对作弊零容忍。

latinEntries.meaning: the empty place in a numeral

definition_zh: 地带；区域；时区；（将……）分成区域
definition_en: an area with a particular purpose or feature, or one of the belts into which the earth is divided
core_image: 地图上一条虚线圈起来的一块，圈内规则一样，圈外换了规矩
scene: 机场广播提醒旅客，过了安检口就进入限制区域。Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
sceneCN: 这里 zone 是「区域」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的划出的一片地方）；句意为上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。地图上虚线围起的一块，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 zone 加 -ing 构成，义为「区划；区域规划」
由 zone 加 -ed 构成，义为「被划成区的」

senses.title: The marked area
senses.definition: an area with a particular purpose or feature, marked off from what is around it
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的或具有特定特征而划出的一片地方
senses.example: Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
senses.exampleCN: 上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。
senses.why: The word came from a Greek noun for a belt or girdle, and a belt around an area is the image behind every later use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「腰带」的名词，围住一片地方的带子就是后来各种用法的画面。

senses.title: The bands of the earth
senses.definition: one of the belts into which the earth is divided by climate, by time, or by latitude
senses.definitionCN: 按气候、时间或纬度把地球划成的带
senses.example: The earth is divided into twenty-four time zones.
senses.exampleCN: 地球被划分为二十四个时区。
senses.why: The oldest use fitted the earth itself, where a wide belt of the globe could be marked off and named.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法直接用在球体上，把地球上一圈宽带划出来命名。

senses.title: The area set aside
senses.definition: an area set aside by law or rule for one use, such as parking, building, or trade
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依规留给某种用途的地片，如停车、建筑或贸易
senses.example: The old harbour became a free trade zone last year.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港区去年成了自由贸易区。
senses.why: A marked strip of land can be reserved by rules, so the belt becomes an official zone with its own regulations.
senses.whyCN: 划出的一条地可以按规则保留，于是这条带子成了有自己的规章的正式区域。

senses.title: To divide into zones
senses.definition: to divide an area into zones, usually for building rules or planning
senses.definitionCN: 把一片地方划成若干区，多用于建筑规则或规划
senses.example: The council zoned the land for housing twenty years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在二十年前就把这片地划作住宅区。
senses.why: The noun turns into an act of drawing the belts on the map, so the same word works as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了在地图上画带子的动作，于是同一个词也能作动词。

senses.title: The space of focus
senses.definition: a state of deep attention, used in phrases such as in the zone, and in zone out for losing attention
senses.definitionCN: 高度集中的状态，见于 in the zone，以及 zone out 表示走神
senses.example: After ten minutes she was in the zone and finished the paper quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 十分钟后她进入了专注状态，很快就写完了卷子。
senses.why: A zone that encloses an area also encloses a mind, so the word stretches from ground to attention.
senses.whyCN: 围住一片地方的区也能围住一个人的心思，于是这个词从地面伸到注意力。

intro.en: Zone comes from Latin zona and Greek zōnē, which both meant a belt worn round the body.
intro.cn: zone 出自拉丁语 zona 与希腊语 zōnē，两者都指缠在身上的腰带。

items.en: zōnē was the word for a belt or girdle, from a verb meaning to gird up.
items.cn: 希腊语 zōnē 指腰带、束带，出自意为「束起」的动词。

items.en: Latin zona kept the meaning of a belt and was also used for a band of the heavens.
items.cn: 拉丁语 zona 保留腰带之义，也用来指天上的一条带。

items.en: Writers used zonae for the belts of climate that circle the earth.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语作者用 zonae 指环抱地球的气候带。

items.en: The word entered English through French, where it meant both a band and a strip of land.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，法语中既指带子也指一条地。

items.en: English applied zone to areas of special rule, then to time zones and to states of mind.
items.cn: 英语把 zone 用到有特殊规则的区域，后用于时区与心理状态。

note.en: Zone is compared with its family and with other words for marked areas.
note.cn: zone 与自己的词族以及其它表示划定区域的词作对照。

entries.definition: the dividing of land into zones
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，区划，区域规划

entries.definition: divided into zones
the quality of a sound, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，音调，词源不同

entries.definition: a part of a place with no fixed border
entries.definitionCN: 近义，一片区域，边界不固定

entries.definition: a large part of a country or the world
a long band of land or climate
entries.definitionCN: 近义，成带的地域，也与词源相关

normalIntro.en: The image of a belt wrapped round the earth explains most of the word's senses.
normalIntro.cn: 一条缠在地球上的带子，解释了这个词的大多数义项。

normal.en: Time zones are belts wrapped round the globe, each one an hour apart.
normal.cn: 时区就是缠在地球上的带子，每条相隔一小时。

normal.en: Zoning is the act of drawing those belts on the map for planning.
normal.cn: zoning 就是在图上为规划画出这些带子。

normal.en: Greek zōnē meant a girdle, and the verb zōnnynai meant to gird up a garment.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zōnē 意为束带，动词 zōnnynai 意为束起衣服。

normal.en: The verb and the noun share a spelling, so land can be zoned into zones.
normal.cn: 动词与名词拼写相同，所以地可以被划成若干 zone。

normal.en: In the zone means absorbed in the work, while zone out means the opposite.
normal.cn: in the zone 指全神贯注，zone out 则相反。

abstract.en: Picture a waist band tightened around the middle of a body, and then around a whole planet.
abstract.cn: 想象一条腰带先系在腰上，然后系住整个星球。

abstract.en: Picture a dashed line on a car park floor, and everything inside it obeys one rule.
abstract.cn: 想象停车场地上一条虚线，线内一切都守同一条规矩。

abstract.en: Picture a radio dial with bands marked out, each playing something different.
abstract.cn: 想象一个刻着分格的收音机旋钮，每一格放不同的内容。

examples.en: Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
examples.cn: 上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。

examples.en: The earth is divided into twenty-four time zones.
examples.cn: 地球被划分为二十四个时区。

examples.en: The council zoned the land for housing twenty years ago.
examples.cn: 议会在二十年前就把这片地划作住宅区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「宗」——老家按宗族分片而居，一宗一片，界线清清楚楚，这种划出来的一片就是 zone。

root: 经由拉丁语 zona 借自希腊语 zōnē（腰带、束带），词根意为「束起」；后由腰带之义扩展为地球上的气候带与时区。

sensesIntro.en: A belt round the body becomes a belt round the earth, then an area with its own rules, an act of dividing land, and finally a state of attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条系在身上的带子先变成环抱地球的带，再变成有自己规则的区域、划分土地的动作，最后成了注意力的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dashed circle drawn on a map
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上画起的一块虚线圆圈

branches.en: The marked area keeps the picture of a band around something.
branches.cn: 划出的区域保留了「围住某物的一条带」这一画面。

branches.en: The earth's belts give climate and time zones.
branches.cn: 地球上的带子给出气候带与时区。

branches.en: Rules attached to a strip of land turn it into an official zone.
branches.cn: 给一条地附上规则，它就变成正式的区域。

branches.en: Drawing the belts becomes an action, so the noun works as a verb.
branches.cn: 画出这些带子成了动作，于是名词也能作动词。

branches.en: A zone around a mind names deep attention or its loss.
branches.cn: 围着心思的区，指专注或走神。

intro.en: Zone takes -ing and -ed, and appears in compounds such as time zone and school zone.
intro.cn: zone 能加 -ing、-ed，也出现在 time zone、school zone 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin zona is a straight borrowing from Greek, and the same root gives English the word girdle through a different path.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 zona 直接借自希腊语，同一词根经另一条路径给出英语的 girdle 一词。

items.example: This is a quiet zone.
items.exampleCN: 这里是安静区。

items.example: Zoning rules limit building height.
items.exampleCN: 分区规划规则限制建筑高度。

items.example: The land is zoned for farming.
items.exampleCN: 这片地被划为农业区。

items.meaning: a belt of the earth with one clock time
items.meaningCN: 使用同一钟时的一片地域
items.example: The country spans three time zones.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家跨越三个时区。

items.meaning: an area with speed limits near a school
items.example: Slow down in the school zone.
items.exampleCN: 在校区要减速。

items.example: Greek zōnē is the source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 zōnē 是这个词的来源。

items.example: Latin zona also names a band of the sky.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 zona 也指天上的一条带。

items.meaning: a belt worn round the waist
items.example: Girdle reached English by another route.
items.exampleCN: girdle 经另一条路径进入英语。
